methods.name: forward
methods.signature: int forward(const int & q, const int & k, const int & v, const int & attn_mask_or_null, double scale, bool is_causal)
methods.summary: Run the SDPA forward and return the output tensor.
methods.extended:
Dispatches to `IBackend::sdpa_forward` after validating that the
leading batch dims of `q`, `k` and `v` agree, that
`q.shape[-1] == k.shape[-1]` (the dot-product key dim `d_k`),
and that `k.shape[-2] == v.shape[-2]` (the source-sequence
length `L_k`).  On the autograd-recording path this also
attaches a new `ScaledDotProductAttentionBackward` node with
`saved_weights_` populated.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Query tensor of shape `(..., L_q, d_k)` with at least 2 dimensions.  All leading "batch" dims must broadcast with the corresponding dims of `k` and `v`.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Key tensor of shape `(..., L_k, d_k)`; the last dim must equal `q.shape[-1]`.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: Value tensor of shape `(..., L_k, d_v)`; the penultimate dim must equal `k.shape[-2]`.

parameters.name: attn_mask_or_null
parameters.description: Optional additive mask broadcastable to `(..., L_q, L_k)`. Pass `nullptr` to omit (no additive term is materialised).

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Multiplicative factor applied to `Q @ K^T` before the softmax.  Typically $1/\sqrt{d_k}$.

parameters.name: is_causal
parameters.description: If `true`, an upper-triangular `-inf` mask is added engine-side, restricting position `i` to attend only to positions `j <= i`.

returns.description: Attention output of shape `(..., L_q, d_v)`.

raises.description: If any input is null, devices or dtypes disagree, rank is less than 2, or the shape contracts above are violated.

methods.name: apply
methods.signature: int apply(int grad_out)
methods.summary: Compute gradients with respect to `Q`, `K`, `V` and the additive mask from the upstream gradient of the output.
methods.extended:
Reconstructs the saved weight matrix on the GPU path (where
`saved_weights_` is a `{1}`-shape placeholder) by recomputing
$W = \text{softmax}(QK^\top \cdot s)$, then dispatches to
`IBackend::sdpa_backward` for the input gradients.

Because the scores are $S = QK^\top s + M$, the mask gradient is
exactly the score gradient: $\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial M =
\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial S$.  Both backends already form that
quantity to produce dQ and dK, so it is returned rather than
discarded, then reduced from the full score shape back to
`orig_mask_shape_`.  A `Bool` keep-mask is not differentiable and
gets no edge.

parameters.name: grad_out
parameters.description: Upstream gradient $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial y$ shaped like the SDPA output `(..., L_q, d_v)`.

returns.description: Four Storage objects in edge order `{dQ, dK, dV, dM}`, reshaped back to `orig_q_shape_` / `orig_k_shape_` / `orig_v_shape_` / `orig_mask_shape_`.  `dM` is empty when no differentiable mask was supplied; the engine discards it because that edge is null.

methods.name: apply_for_graph
methods.signature: int apply_for_graph(const int & grad_out)
methods.summary: Graph-recording backward for `create_graph=True`.
methods.extended:
The fused backward returns Storages, so a second derivative through
attention — a gradient penalty, the double-backward form of a JVP —
had nothing to differentiate.  This writes the closed form out in
recording ops, recomputing the weights from the saved `Q` and `K`
under the same mask the forward used.

parameters.name: grad_out
parameters.description: Upstream gradient, possibly carrying its own `grad_fn`.

returns.description: `{dQ, dK, dV, dM}`; `dM` is null unless the additive mask is a differentiable input.

members.summary: Autograd node for scaled dot-product attention with optional additive mask and post-softmax causal constraint.
members.extended:
Implements the canonical SDPA operation from [Vaswani et al. (2017)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762),
$\text{Attn}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M\right)V$,
where $Q, K, V$ are query / key / value projections shaped
`(..., L, D)` and $M$ is an additive mask (`-inf` at disallowed
positions, `0` elsewhere).  The node saves three edges
`{Q, K, V}` and a fourth Storage slot `saved_weights_` holding the
pre-multiplication attention weight matrix
$W = \text{softmax}(QK^\top \cdot s)$, where `s = scale_`.

On the MLX (GPU) path the fused `mlx::core::fast::scaled_dot_product_attention`
kernel does not return $W$ — instead it returns a `{1}`-shape
placeholder.  `apply()` detects `saved_weights_.shape().size() == 1`
and re-computes $W = \text{softmax}(QK^\top \cdot s)$ from the saved
$Q, K$ before back-propagating.  On the Accelerate (CPU) path the
kernel returns the genuine weight matrix and the recompute branch is
skipped.

**Math**

$$
  A_{ij} = s \cdot (Q_i \cdot K_j), \quad
  P_{ij} = \frac{\exp(A_{ij} + M_{ij})}{\sum_k \exp(A_{ik} + M_{ik})}, \quad
  y_i = \sum_j P_{ij}\, V_j
$$
Gradients flow back through the softmax Jacobian
$\partial P / \partial A = \mathrm{diag}(P) - P P^\top$ (per row),
giving
$$
  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial Q} = s \cdot (\Delta A)\, K,\quad
  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial K} = s \cdot (\Delta A)^\top Q,\quad
  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial V} = P^\top\, \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial y}
$$
where $\Delta A_{ij} = P_{ij}\bigl(\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial y_i \cdot V_j^\top - \sum_k P_{ik} (\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial y_i \cdot V_k^\top)\bigr)$.

**References**

Vaswani et al., "Attention Is All You Need" (NeurIPS 2017).
notes:
The mask is *additive*: callers must already have converted boolean
"where to mask" patterns into floats containing `-inf` where the
position should be excluded and `0` elsewhere (see
`lucid.nn.modules.attention._to_additive_mask`).  Causal masking
is implemented engine-side when `is_causal=true` by adding an
upper-triangular `-inf` matrix before the softmax, so the caller
does not need to materialise the mask in Python.

members.summary: Combined determinism + AMP dtype-resolution guard.

constructor performs both checks; subsequent code reads the resolved
dtype via `effective_dtype`.

on the op's device until the guard is destroyed, so it must live as long
as the op's body.  Outside one it owns nothing.

members.summary: Autograd node for SELU (Scaled ELU, Klambauer et al. 2017).
members.extended:
Uses the self-normalising constants $\alpha \approx 1.6732632$ and
$\lambda \approx 1.0507010$ baked into the backend; the Python and C++
layers do not expose them to the caller.  The backward delegates to the
backend because the piecewise scaled-ELU formula depends on those fixed
constants.

**Math**

$$y = \lambda\,\begin{cases} x, & x \ge 0 \\
                             \alpha\,(e^x - 1), & x < 0 \end{cases}$$

**References**

Klambauer et al., "Self-Normalizing Neural Networks", [arXiv:1706.02515](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.02515).

methods.name: cpu_view
methods.signature: CpuStorage cpu_view()
methods.summary: Returns a `CpuStorage` that aliases `cpu_ptr` without copying bytes.
methods.extended:
The returned storage installs a custom deleter that holds a copy of
`owner`, guaranteeing the Metal buffer outlives every
`CpuStorage` view spawned this way.  The `VersionCounter`
is also shared with this `SharedStorage`, so mutations through
the CPU view are visible to the GPU side.

returns.description: CPU view aliasing the shared buffer.  Lifetime-tied to `owner`.

members.summary: Metal shared-memory storage accessible from both CPU and GPU.
members.extended:
The underlying allocation is a Metal buffer created with
`MTLResourceStorageModeShared`, which the Metal driver maps into the
process address space.  This gives Lucid a zero-copy host↔device bridge on
Apple Silicon unified-memory hardware: the same bytes are addressable from
CPU code through `cpu_ptr` and submitted to the GPU through
`mtl_handle`.

**See Also**

`cpu_view` — produces a `CpuStorage` aliasing this buffer.
notes:
A `TensorImpl` never holds this variant at rest.  Its constructor
keeps the descriptor aside and stores the `cpu_view` or the GPU alias
its device label calls for, so every op sees ordinary storage.

attributes.name: cpu_ptr
attributes.description: Host-side mapped pointer.  Safe to dereference from any CPU thread.

attributes.name: mtl_handle
attributes.description: Opaque `id<MTLBuffer>` handle, stored as `void*` to avoid pulling the Metal headers into this translation unit.

attributes.name: nbytes
attributes.description: Allocation capacity in bytes.

attributes.name: dtype
attributes.description: Element type.  Default `Dtype::F32`.

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Shared mutation counter — same semantics as the other variants.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.description: Lifetime token for the underlying Metal allocation.  The `cpu_view` deleter captures a copy so the Metal buffer cannot be freed while a CPU view is alive.

attributes.name: gpu_alias
attributes.description: The one MLX external array over the buffer, shared by every copy of this descriptor.  GPU aliases are copies of it, so MLX never sees an alias as the sole owner of the buffer and cannot donate the buffer to an op's output — which would write the result into memory the CPU side is still reading.  Set by `gpu::pin_shared_storage` when a tensor first adopts the buffer.

members.summary: Autograd node for the logistic sigmoid $y = 1 / (1 + e^{-x})$.
members.extended:
Saves the *output* $y$ rather than the input because the gradient formula
$y(1 - y)$ depends only on $y$.  This avoids a redundant forward pass and
keeps the saved tensor at the same dtype as the activation.

**Math**

$$y = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-x}}, \qquad \frac{\partial y}{\partial x} = y\,(1 - y)$$
notes:
The eager backward builds $(1 - y)$ via `mul_scalar(-1) + add_scalar(1)`
to reuse the existing storage primitives rather than introducing a dedicated
subtract kernel.

members.extended:
Saves the input `x` so the backward pass can evaluate $\cosh(x)$ and
scale the upstream gradient by it.  Defined on all of $\mathbb{R}$ with
the identity $\sinh(x) = (e^x - e^{-x})/2$.

**Math**

$$y = \sinh(x), \qquad

\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x} =

notes:

Output magnitude grows exponentially; large-magnitude inputs can overflow
to `+inf` / `-inf`.

methods.summary: Eager-mode backward: dispatches to `IBackend::softmax_backward` which evaluates $p \odot (\partial L/\partial y - \langle p, \partial L/\partial y\rangle)$ in a single fused pass along `axis_`.

methods.name: apply_for_graph
methods.signature: int apply_for_graph(const int & grad_out)
methods.summary: Graph-mode backward.  Recomputes the forward from the saved input rather than reusing the saved output Storage: the adjoint depends on that output, so a data-only stand-in would silently drop the whole d(out)/d(in) path from the second derivative.

members.summary: Autograd node for the numerically stable softmax along a single axis $p_i = e^{x_i - m} / \sum_j e^{x_j - m}$ with $m = \max_j x_j$.
members.extended:
Subtracting the per-row maximum $m$ before exponentiating is the standard
log-sum-exp trick — it preserves the analytic result while keeping every
exponentiated term in $(0, 1]$, which is essential under `ForceFP32`
AMP semantics for fp16/bf16 logits.  The softmax probabilities $p$ are
saved on the node so the backward needs no re-evaluation.

**Math**

$$p_i = \frac{e^{x_i}}{\sum_j e^{x_j}},
  \qquad \frac{\partial L}{\partial x_i}
  = p_i\,\Bigl(\frac{\partial L}{\partial y_i}
               - \sum_j p_j\,\frac{\partial L}{\partial y_j}\Bigr)$$

The Jacobian-vector form sidesteps materialising the dense
$N \times N$ softmax Jacobian and runs in $O(N)$ per row.

**Shape**

Input and output share the same shape; the normalisation contracts only
along `axis_`.  Negative axis values are normalised to non-negative
indices by `forward` before being stored.

**References**

Bishop, "Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning", §4.3.4.

raises.description: If the normalised axis falls outside `[0, ndim)`.

attributes.description: Canonical (non-negative) axis along which the softmax is computed.

attributes.name: saved_output_

methods.name: apply
methods.signature: int apply(int grad_out)
methods.summary: Compute input gradients for the forward solve $AX = B$.

parameters.name: grad_out
parameters.description: Upstream gradient $G = \partial L / \partial X$, shaped like the forward output $X$.

returns.description: Two-element vector `{dA, dB}` matching the input ordering `[A=0, B=1]` that `NaryKernel` expects, where `dB = solve(Aᵀ, G)` and `dA = -dB @ Xᵀ`.

notes:
The transpose solve `solve(Aᵀ, G)` performs a fresh LU
factorisation of $A^\top$ — the forward factors are not cached.

methods.name: apply_for_graph
methods.signature: int apply_for_graph(const int & grad_out)
methods.summary: The same adjoint solve, recorded, with X recomputed from A and B.

members.summary: Autograd node for the general linear solve $AX = B$.
members.extended:
Wired on the operands after the shape contract aligned them —
`(batch, N, N)` and `(batch, N, K)` — so it never sees a vector or a
broadcast.  The forward saves $A$ as `saved_inputs_[0]` (required to
build $A^\top$ for the adjoint solve) and the solution $X$ as
`saved_output_` (required for the outer-product step that yields
$\partial L / \partial A$).

**Math**

Given upstream gradient $G = \partial L / \partial X$:
$$
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial B} = \text{solve}(A^\top, G), \qquad
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial A} = -\,\frac{\partial L}{\partial B}\, X^\top
$$
Both expressions compose existing differentiable ops
([[solve_op]] / [[matmul_op]] / [[neg_op]] / [[mT_op]]) so that
second-order gradients flow automatically.

**References**

Giles, "Collected Matrix Derivative Results for Forward and Reverse
Mode Algorithmic Differentiation" (Oxford, 2008), §2.4.

attributes.name: schema_v1
attributes.description: `"solve"`, one saved-input slot, `AmpPolicy::KeepInput` — prevents a lossy autocast promotion before the LAPACK call.

methods.name: apply
methods.signature: int apply(int grad_out)

methods.name: apply_for_graph
methods.signature: int apply_for_graph(const int & grad_out)

members.summary: Autograd node for the triangular solve $AX = B$, wired on the operands the shape contract aligned (`(batch, N, N)` and `(batch, N, K)`).
members.extended:
With $G = \partial L / \partial X$:
$$
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial B} = A^{-\top} G, \qquad
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial A} = \Pi\!\left(-\frac{\partial L}{\partial B}\, X^\top\right)
$$
where $\Pi$ keeps the triangle the forward read — the upper one when
`upper_`, and without the diagonal when `unitriangular_` (that
diagonal is assumed, not read, so it takes no gradient).  $A^\top$ is
triangular the other way round, so the adjoint is one more triangular
solve; every step is a recorded op, so the result differentiates again.

methods.name: dispatch
methods.signature: int dispatch(backend::IBackend & be, const int & a, const int & shape, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: Forward — calls `IBackend::sqrt` to compute $y = \sqrt{x}$.

methods.signature: int grad_formula(const int & g)
methods.summary: Backward — $\partial y/\partial x = 1/(2y)$, scaled by `grad_out`.

methods.name: grad_formula_impl
methods.signature: int grad_formula_impl(const int & g, const int &, const int & out)
methods.summary: Graph-mode backward: $\partial x = g / (2y)$ where $y = \sqrt{x}$ is the saved output; kept inside the autograd graph.

members.summary: Autograd node for the element-wise square root $y = \sqrt{x}$.
members.extended:
Saves the *output* $y$ because the backward formula
$\partial y / \partial x = 1 / (2y)$ is cheaper and numerically
identical to recomputing $\sqrt{x}$.  Defined for $x \geq 0$; negative
inputs produce NaN.

**Math**

$$y = \sqrt{x}, \qquad
\frac{\partial y}{\partial x} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{1}{2y},
\qquad
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x} =
\frac{1}{2y}\,\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial y}, \quad x \geq 0.$$
notes:
Dispatch: a correctly rounded root on CPU (`vvsqrt` for F64, a plain loop
for F32 because `vvsqrtf` is not exact — backend/cpu/Vforce.cpp) / MLX
`sqrt` (GPU).
Gradient is unbounded as $x \to 0^+$.

methods.summary: Compute the storage-level gradients for both operands.

parameters.description: Forward inputs (unused — values irrelevant to subtraction gradient).

members.summary: Autograd node for element-wise subtraction $y = a - b$ with NumPy broadcasting.
members.extended:
Inherits forward dispatch, broadcasting logic, and the apply() trampoline
from BinaryOp<SubBackward>.  No forward inputs are saved because the
gradient depends only on the upstream gradient: $a$ receives it unchanged
and $b$ receives it negated.  Broadcast-reduces each branch back to the
original input shape via `sum_to_shape` inside
`BinaryKernel::apply`.

**Math**

$$
  y = a - b, \qquad
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial a} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial y}, \qquad
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial b} = -\frac{\partial L}{\partial y}
$$

**Shape**

Inputs follow NumPy broadcasting; output has the broadcasted shape.  Each
gradient is then reduced to the original input's shape.

**See Also**

AddBackward, MulBackward, DivBackward
notes:
CPU dispatch uses Accelerate `vDSP_vsub` / `vDSP_vsubD` for F32 / F64.
GPU dispatch uses MLX's broadcast-aware `subtract` primitive.

attributes.description: `false` — gradient is value-independent.

members.summary: Autograd node for the multi-axis reduction sum $y = \sum_{i \in \text{axes}} x_i$.
members.extended:
The gradient broadcasts unchanged from the reduced shape back to the
input shape because $\partial y / \partial x_i = 1$ for every element
participating in the sum.  `kSavesInput = false` and no output is
saved — the rule is independent of both the forward input and output.

**Math**

$$
  y = \sum_{i \in \text{axes}} x_i, \qquad
  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x_i} =
  \mathrm{broadcast}\!\left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial y}
  \right).
$$
notes:
Dispatch: Accelerate strided reductions (CPU) / MLX `sum` (GPU).
For empty reductions the output is $0$ (additive identity).

members.summary: Autograd node for element-wise tangent $y = \tan(x)$.
members.extended:
Saves the input `x` so the backward pass can build $\cos^2(x)$ in the
denominator.  Defined for all real $x$ except the singular points
$x = (k + \tfrac{1}{2})\pi$ where $\cos x = 0$; behaviour at those
points is undefined.

**Math**

$$y = \tan(x), \qquad
\frac{\partial y}{\partial x} = \sec^2(x) = \frac{1}{\cos^2(x)}, \qquad
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x} =
\frac{1}{\cos^2(x)}\,\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial y}.$$
notes: Dispatch: Accelerate `vvtanf`/`vvtan` (CPU) / MLX `tan` (GPU).

methods.summary: Forward — calls `IBackend::tanh` to compute $y = \tanh x$.

methods.summary: Backward — $\partial y/\partial x = 1 - y^2$ using the saved output, scaled by `grad_out`.

methods.signature: int grad_formula_impl(const int & g, const int &, const int & out)
methods.summary: Graph-mode backward: $\partial x = (1 - \mathrm{out}^2) \cdot g$ where $\mathrm{out} = \tanh x$; kept inside the autograd graph.

members.summary: Autograd node for element-wise hyperbolic tangent $y = \tanh(x)$.
members.extended:
Saves the *output* $y$ rather than the input because the backward
formula $1 - y^2$ is cheaper than re-evaluating $\tanh(x)$ and avoids a
second `vvtanhf` pass.  `kSavesInput = false` opts out of the
default input-save behaviour and `kSavesOutput = true` registers the
output instead.  Range is $(-1, 1)$ on all of $\mathbb{R}$.

**Math**

$$y = \tanh(x), \qquad
\frac{\partial y}{\partial x} = 1 - \tanh^2(x) = 1 - y^2, \qquad
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x} =
(1 - y^2)\,\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial y}.$$
notes: Dispatch: Accelerate `vvtanhf`/`vvtanh` (CPU) / MLX `tanh` (GPU).

methods.name: TensorImpl
methods.signature: void TensorImpl(int storage, int shape, Dtype dtype, Device device, bool requires_grad)
methods.summary: Constructs a `TensorImpl` from an already-allocated `Storage`.
methods.extended:
The C-contiguous (row-major) stride is computed automatically from
`shape` and `dtype`.  When `requires_grad` is `true` an
`AutogradMeta` is constructed immediately; otherwise it is
left unallocated until needed.

parameters.name: storage
parameters.description: Backing memory (any variant).  Ownership is moved in.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Dimension vector.  May be empty for a scalar.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: CPU or GPU.  Must match the variant of `storage`.

parameters.name: requires_grad
parameters.description: Whether the tensor should track gradients from the start.

methods.name: from_numpy
methods.signature: int from_numpy(int arr, Device device, bool requires_grad)
methods.summary: Constructs a `TensorImpl` by copying data from a NumPy array.
methods.extended:
The data is always copied into a fresh `CpuStorage` buffer.
When `device == Device::GPU` the buffer is subsequently uploaded
to MLX via the GPU bridge, yielding a `GpuStorage`-backed
tensor.

parameters.name: arr
parameters.description: Source NumPy array.  Must be a signed / floating / complex dtype.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Target device for the constructed tensor.

parameters.name: requires_grad
parameters.description: Whether the resulting tensor tracks gradients.

returns.description: Newly constructed tensor.

raises.description: The array has an unsigned dtype.  The caller must cast to a signed integer or floating-point type first.

methods.name: storage
methods.signature: const int & storage()
methods.summary: The backing `Storage`, as a dense row-major buffer of exactly this tensor's elements.
methods.extended:
Nearly every op hands `storage()` straight to a backend kernel that
reads it as dense, from its first byte.  A CPU view at an offset or
with strides read the wrong bytes there — about a hundred ops did, and
the audit's layout axis found them once it fed them real views.  So a
non-dense CPU tensor answers with a packed copy of the elements it
reads, rebuilt whenever its version moves (a write through it or
through any member of its view family).  Every other tensor answers
with its own buffer, as before.

A member of a Metal view family answers with its elements read out of
the family's root, cached the same way — or with the root itself when
it reads all of it, in the root's shape.

Code that walks the geometry itself — `contiguous`, the NumPy bridge,
`data_ptr`, buffer-identity and overlap tests — reads
`raw_storage` instead.

methods.name: raw_storage
methods.signature: const int & raw_storage()
methods.summary: The backing `Storage` as it is, before any packing: the whole buffer a view reads into, to be walked with `stride` and `storage_offset`.  For a Metal family member, the family's root.

methods.name: mutable_storage
methods.signature: int & mutable_storage()
methods.summary: Returns a mutable reference to the backing `Storage` variant.
methods.extended:
Used by engine writers that replace the values wholesale (the C++
optimisers, BatchNorm's running statistics, the compiled step);
callers are responsible for bumping the version counter when they
mutate the underlying bytes.  A Metal family member that reads its
whole root hands out the root itself, reshaped to this tensor's shape,
so what the caller writes is what every member reads.

raises.description: The tensor is a Metal view of part of its family's root, which a wholesale replacement cannot write.

methods.name: check_wholesale_writable
methods.signature: void check_wholesale_writable(const char * name)
methods.summary: Refuses, before anything is written, a tensor `mutable_storage` would refuse: a Metal view of part of its family's root.  A writer that updates several tensors in one step checks them all first, so a refusal leaves every one of them — and the writer's own state — as it was.

raises.description: The tensor is a Metal view of part of its family's root.

methods.name: family_key
methods.signature: const void * family_key()
methods.summary: An identity shared by every member of this tensor's Metal view family and by nothing else — where autograd measures a member's elements from when it re-derives the family after a write — or `nullptr` when the tensor is not a Metal family member.

methods.name: family_id
methods.signature: int family_id()
methods.summary: Stable non-zero identity shared by every member of this tensor's view family (on both CPU and Metal), or `0` when the tensor belongs to no view family.

methods.name: storage_offset
methods.signature: int storage_offset()
methods.summary: Returns the byte offset of this tensor's first element from the start of `raw_storage` (the handle coordinate frame).
methods.extended:
Rule: anything that shows a position or size to the user, or takes one
from the user (`storage_offset`, `untyped_storage`, `as_strided`),
uses the allocation coordinate frame (`allocation_offset`,
`allocation_nbytes`, `allocation_base`).  `storage_offset`
and `raw_storage` are the handle frame for code that walks bytes.

returns.description: `0` for owning tensors and block views; non-zero for strided views created with `make_view`.

methods.name: allocation_offset
methods.signature: int allocation_offset()
methods.summary: Byte offset of this tensor's first element from the start of the underlying allocation (the user-facing storage coordinate frame).

methods.name: allocation_nbytes
methods.signature: int allocation_nbytes()
methods.summary: Total byte size of the underlying allocation (the user-facing storage capacity).

methods.name: allocation_base
methods.signature: int allocation_base()
methods.summary: Host/device base address of the start of the underlying allocation.

methods.name: storage_is_shared
methods.signature: bool storage_is_shared()
methods.summary: Predicate: is this tensor's CPU storage aliased by another tensor?

returns.description: `true` when the underlying `CpuStorage` `ptr` is referenced by more than one `shared_ptr` — i.e. at least one other view of this tensor exists.  Always `false` for `GpuStorage` and `SharedStorage` variants (those variants do not currently report sharing through this hook).

methods.name: is_phantom
methods.signature: bool is_phantom()
methods.summary: Predicate: is this a phantom tensor — shape, dtype, device and autograd state, and a `PhantomStorage` in place of values?
methods.extended:
Made by every factory and op while `PhantomMode` is on.  A
phantom stays one after the mode is off: the kernels take it as an
input and give a phantom back, and a read of its values raises.  It is
never a Metal family member, so its own storage is its storage.

methods.name: views_by_stride
methods.signature: bool views_by_stride()
methods.summary: Predicate: does a view of this tensor keep its strides over the same buffer — the CPU's rule?  A Metal tensor views through its family's root, or copies.  A phantom follows its device, so its views have the strides, and a `view` the refusals, of the tensor it stands in for.

methods.name: is_aliased
methods.signature: bool is_aliased()
methods.summary: Predicate: does another live tensor read this one's buffer as a view of it — a member of the same `ViewFamily`?
methods.extended:
Such a tensor is written in place rather than handed a new storage
slot, so its views see the write (`write_through`).  Unlike
`storage_is_shared`, a NumPy array or a storage saved for
backward does not count: neither is a view.

returns.description: `true` while at least one other member of the family is alive.

methods.name: is_detached_alias
methods.signature: bool is_detached_alias()
methods.summary: Predicate: is this a detached alias — what `.data` hands out — rather than a view autograd follows?  Other clone_with_grad aliases are not detached: a factory's `requires_grad=True` tensor is one, and it has to stay an ordinary member once the temporary it aliased is gone.
methods.extended:
It reads the same buffer as the rest of its family and shares their
version counter, but a write through it is untracked by design: the
values change and no graph is re-derived, as with the reference's
`.data`.  Reshape-family views are not detached.

methods.name: set_detached_alias
methods.signature: void set_detached_alias(bool v)
methods.summary: Marks this tensor as a detached alias; see `is_detached_alias`.

methods.name: is_custom_function_output
methods.signature: bool is_custom_function_output()
methods.summary: Predicate: is this tensor a view returned as an output of a tracked custom `Function`?  In-place writes directly into such a view are refused while grad mode is enabled, and in-place writes into its base or another view of its family invalidate its `grad_fn` (LCD-558).

methods.name: set_custom_function_output
methods.signature: void set_custom_function_output(bool v)
methods.summary: Marks this tensor as a custom `Function` output view.

methods.name: views_grad_leaf
methods.signature: bool views_grad_leaf()
methods.summary: Predicate: was this tensor made, through any chain of views, from a live leaf that requires grad?
methods.extended:
A write through such a view moves the leaf's values, so autograd
refuses it as it refuses a write to the leaf itself.  Only the bases
the chain passes through count, as in the reference: writing the
leaf's own base, or a view made beside the leaf, is allowed.  A
detached alias ends the chain, since its writes are untracked.

methods.name: rederived_by_family_writes
methods.signature: bool rederived_by_family_writes()
methods.summary: Predicate: does a write into this tensor's family re-derive this member's graph (inplace::rebase_views)?
methods.extended:
Not for a detached alias, which autograd does not follow, and not for
a leaf that requires grad: gradient accumulates there, so the leaf
keeps its place and only its values move.

methods.name: write_through
methods.signature: void write_through(const TensorImpl & src, const char * name)
methods.summary: Writes `src`'s values into this tensor's buffer, in place.
methods.extended:
The write an in-place op makes to a tensor with live views: into the
bytes the views read, where a new storage slot would leave them
reading the old ones.  A Metal family member writes into the family's
root instead.  Bumps the version, which every member shares.

parameters.name: src
parameters.description: The new values; same shape and dtype.

raises.description: `src` has another shape.

`src` has another dtype, a view of a leaf that requires grad would be modified while autograd records, the elements overlap and `name` is not `fill_`, or the buffer is a gradient's that something else also reads.

The tensor is on the GPU outside a view family; or its CPU buffer is also held by something that is not one of its views — a storage saved for backward, a NumPy array — which would read the new values without being told; or autograd would have to re-derive a strided Metal view after the write, which it cannot yet.

methods.name: metal_shared
methods.signature: const SharedStorage * metal_shared()
methods.summary: The Metal shared buffer this tensor still is, or `nullptr`.
methods.extended:
Non-null only while the storage is the whole buffer, contiguous from
its first byte in its own dtype — the one case a relabel to the other
device can alias rather than copy.  `nullptr` for views that cover
less, and once an op has replaced the storage.

returns.description: The descriptor, or `nullptr`.

methods.name: take_storage_from
methods.signature: void take_storage_from(TensorImpl & out, const char * name)
methods.summary: Take `out`'s contents after an in-place op.
methods.extended:
Ordinarily a swap of the storage *slot* — see
`ops/utils/InplaceGraph.h` for why the slot and not the buffer.
A tensor over a Metal shared buffer writes the new values into the
buffer instead, so every alias of it sees them — but only when `out`
recorded no graph, since a node that saved the pre-op input shares the
buffer.  A CPU tensor with live views always writes into its buffer
(`write_through`), and so does one read from `.grad`
(`grad_to_tensor`), whose buffer is its owner's gradient.
Otherwise the swap happens and the tensor stops being shared.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The op's result; its storage is moved from.

raises.description: The tensor is a CPU tensor whose elements overlap (an expanded view), or a gradient's buffer that something else also reads.

methods.name: write_lands_in_buffer
methods.signature: bool write_lands_in_buffer()
methods.summary: Predicate: would an in-place op that records a graph write into the bytes this tensor reads now, rather than hand it a new storage slot?
methods.extended:
The two cases `take_storage_from` writes through: a CPU tensor
with live views, and a tensor read from `.grad` whose write is let
into its gradient's buffer.  An op that keeps a handle on the pre-write
tensor for backward needs to know, because a handle sharing those bytes
would read the new values back — and, for the gradient, would itself be
one more reader that has the write refused.

returns.description: `true` when the write lands in this tensor's current buffer.

methods.name: make_view
methods.signature: int make_view(const int & base, int shape, int stride, int offset_bytes, bool join_family)
methods.summary: Creates a new `TensorImpl` that aliases `base`'s `Storage` with a different shape, stride, and optional byte offset.
methods.extended:
No data is copied.  The view starts with no autograd state of its
own; a caller that makes a differentiable view wires its grad_fn.  The
view joins `base`'s `ViewFamily` — one version counter,
in-place writes into the buffer (on Metal, into the family's root) —
unless `join_family` is `false`; a Metal view outside the family
takes `base`'s elements under its geometry as a value of its own.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: Tensor whose storage the view aliases.

parameters.name: stride
parameters.description: Byte-stride vector for the new view.  Need not be contiguous.

parameters.name: offset_bytes
parameters.description: Byte offset from `base`'s storage origin.  Defaults to `0`.

parameters.name: join_family
parameters.description: Whether the view joins `base`'s family.  Defaults to `true`.

returns.description: New view tensor sharing `base`'s storage.

methods.name: make_dtype_view
methods.signature: int make_dtype_view(const int & base, Dtype dtype, int shape, int stride, int offset_bytes, bool join_family)
methods.summary: Creates a dtype-reinterpreting view over `base`'s storage (used by `real`, `imag`, `view_as_real`, and `view_as_complex`).

methods.name: make_block_view
methods.signature: int make_block_view(const int & base, int shape, int byte_offset)
methods.summary: A view of a contiguous run of `base`'s buffer: `byte_offset` bytes in, `shape`'s elements long — what a leading-dimension slice reads.
methods.extended:
Its storage points at the run itself (an aliasing `shared_ptr` into
`base`'s buffer, sharing its ownership), so the view is dense and
every op reads it from its first byte, as it reads any tensor.  It
joins `base`'s `ViewFamily`.  `base` must be a dense CPU
tensor and the run must lie inside its buffer.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: Dense CPU tensor whose buffer the view reads.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Shape of the view; its elements are the run's, in order.

parameters.name: byte_offset
parameters.description: Where the run starts in `base`'s storage.

returns.description: The view, with no autograd state of its own.

methods.name: make_allocation_view
methods.signature: int make_allocation_view(const int & base, int shape, int stride, int allocation_byte_offset)
methods.summary: Creates a view over `base`'s full underlying allocation at `allocation_byte_offset` bytes from the allocation start.
methods.extended:
Used by `as_strided_op` so a window taken from a narrowed CPU block
view (or a Metal engine view-family member) can address any element of
the root allocation while remaining in `base`'s `ViewFamily`.

methods.name: meta
methods.signature: const TensorMeta & meta()
methods.summary: Returns a const reference to the `TensorMeta` bundle.

methods.name: shape
methods.signature: const int & shape()
methods.summary: Returns the shape vector.  Backs the Python `.shape` attribute.

methods.name: stride
methods.signature: const int & stride()
methods.summary: Returns the byte-stride vector.  Backs the Python `.stride()` method.

methods.name: dtype
methods.signature: Dtype dtype()
methods.summary: Returns the element dtype.  Backs the Python `.dtype` attribute.

methods.name: device
methods.signature: Device device()
methods.summary: Returns the device tag.  Backs the Python `.device` attribute.

methods.name: requires_grad
methods.signature: bool requires_grad()
methods.summary: Returns the current `requires_grad` flag.

returns.description: `false` when there is no `AutogradMeta` at all (the common inference path — avoids an indirection).

methods.name: is_leaf
methods.signature: bool is_leaf()
methods.summary: Returns the leaf-status flag.
methods.extended:
A *leaf* tensor was constructed directly by the user; a non-leaf
tensor is the output of a differentiable op and carries a non-null
`grad_fn`.

returns.description: `true` for leaves, `true` (default) when there is no `AutogradMeta` yet.

methods.name: version
methods.signature: int version()
methods.summary: Returns the autograd version counter.
methods.extended:
Bumped by `bump_version` on every in-place mutation; autograd
snapshots this at forward time and checks it at backward time to
catch illegal mutations.  A tensor over a Metal shared buffer adds the
buffer's own counter, which every alias of the buffer bumps — so a
write through the CPU view invalidates a GPU alias saved for backward,
and the other way round.

returns.description: Current version.  `0` for a tensor that nothing has written in place — no `AutogradMeta` exists until something does (`bump_version`) or the tensor joins a graph.

methods.name: grad_fn
methods.signature: const int & grad_fn()
methods.summary: Returns the backward function pointer for this tensor.

returns.description: Non-null for non-leaf tensors produced by a differentiable op, `nullptr` for leaves and tensors with no `AutogradMeta`.

methods.name: grad_output_nr
methods.signature: int grad_output_nr()
methods.summary: Returns the output index that connects this tensor to its `grad_fn`.
methods.extended:
Multi-output ops produce several tensors that share one
`Node`; this index tells the backward pass which of the
node's outputs the tensor corresponds to.

returns.description: Output index, or `0` when no `AutogradMeta` exists.

methods.name: grad_storage
methods.signature: const int & grad_storage()
methods.summary: Returns the accumulated gradient `Storage`, if any.

returns.description: `std::nullopt` when no gradient has been accumulated, or when the tensor has no `AutogradMeta` at all.

methods.name: mutable_grad_storage
methods.signature: int & mutable_grad_storage()
methods.summary: Returns a mutable reference to the gradient `Storage`, constructing the `AutogradMeta` on demand.
methods.extended: Used by the engine's gradient accumulation paths.

returns.description: Mutable reference; the optional may still be empty even though `AutogradMeta` is now allocated.

methods.name: set_dtype
methods.signature: void set_dtype(Dtype dt)
methods.summary: Sets the dtype field.  Does not touch the underlying bytes; used by pure metadata reinterpretation paths.

methods.name: set_device
methods.signature: void set_device(Device dv)
methods.summary: Sets the device field.  Does not move data; used after an in-place device transfer has updated `storage_`.

methods.name: set_requires_grad
methods.signature: void set_requires_grad(bool v)
methods.summary: Enables or disables gradient tracking.
methods.extended:
Constructs `AutogradMeta` lazily when `v` is `true`.
Setting to `false` does not destroy an already-existing
`AutogradMeta` — only the flag is cleared, so historical
version counters / saved tensors remain valid.

methods.name: set_leaf
methods.signature: void set_leaf(bool v)
methods.summary: Sets the leaf-status flag, constructing `AutogradMeta` if it does not yet exist.

methods.name: set_grad_fn
methods.signature: void set_grad_fn(int fn)
methods.summary: Attaches the backward function pointer.
methods.extended:
Marks the tensor as non-leaf (callers usually pair this with
`set_leaf(false)`).

parameters.name: fn
parameters.description: Backward node produced by the forward-time op kernel.

methods.name: set_grad_output_nr
methods.signature: void set_grad_output_nr(int nr)
methods.summary: Sets the output index associated with `grad_fn`.

parameters.name: nr
parameters.description: Zero-based output index within the producing `Node`.

methods.name: clear_grad_fn
methods.signature: void clear_grad_fn()
methods.summary: Drops the backward function pointer without removing the `AutogradMeta`.
methods.extended:
Used when an in-place op detaches a tensor from the autograd graph
(`tensor.detach_()`-style semantics).

methods.name: data_alias
methods.signature: int data_alias()
methods.summary: Returns the alias `.data` hands out: a member of this tensor's view family with `detached_alias_` set so writes through it are untracked.

methods.name: clone_with_grad
methods.signature: int clone_with_grad(bool requires_grad)
methods.summary: Returns a new TensorImpl sharing the same storage and view family with the requested `requires_grad` flag and no `grad_fn`.

methods.name: detach_inplace
methods.signature: void detach_inplace()
methods.summary: Detaches this TensorImpl in place from the autograd graph so every holder of the same TensorImpl (including `p.grad`) sees `grad_fn` cleared and `requires_grad` set to `false`.

methods.name: custom_function_view
methods.signature: int custom_function_view(bool tracked)
methods.summary: Returns a view of this TensorImpl used when a custom `Function` returns an input as-is (or returns the same tensor twice).

methods.name: saved_output_storage
methods.signature: int saved_output_storage()
methods.summary: Returns a Storage snapshot suitable for saving this TensorImpl as an op's output on a backward node: on the CPU, splits `CpuStorage::ptr` onto a separate control block so subsequent in-place ops on this tensor are not refused as shared storage before the version check at backward.

methods.name: version_sink
methods.signature: int version_sink()
methods.summary: Returns a shared version counter that tracks every in-place version bump on this tensor (and its view family) even after this TensorImpl dies.

methods.name: rebind_version_from
methods.signature: void rebind_version_from(TensorImpl & old)
methods.summary: Bumps `old`'s version counter for an in-place rebind and carries the bumped version (and any saved-output version baseline on this tensor's `grad_fn`) onto this tensor.

methods.name: set_grad_storage
methods.signature: void set_grad_storage(int grad)
methods.summary: Stores a gradient `Storage` directly.

parameters.name: grad
parameters.description: Gradient buffer to adopt.  Must have the same dtype / device / shape as this tensor.

methods.name: install_grad
methods.signature: void install_grad(const int & g, int slot)
methods.summary: Installs an assigned gradient tensor `g` and its validated `slot` buffer on this tensor, keeping `g`'s Metal view family attached so subsequent in-place writes through `.grad` alias `g`.

methods.name: grad_as_impl
methods.signature: int grad_as_impl()
methods.summary: Returns the graph-mode gradient as a full `TensorImpl`.
methods.extended:
Populated when `backward(create_graph=True)` was called — allowing
the gradient itself to participate in further autograd (Hessian-vector
products, MAML, second-order ops).

returns.description: The graph-mode gradient tensor, or `nullptr` when no graph-mode gradient has been accumulated.

methods.name: set_grad_impl
methods.signature: void set_grad_impl(int g)
methods.summary: Sets the graph-mode gradient tensor.

methods.name: accumulate_grad_impl
methods.signature: void accumulate_grad_impl(int g)
methods.summary: Accumulates a graph-mode gradient.
methods.extended:
First call sets the gradient outright; subsequent calls add `g`
into the existing `grad_as_impl` via the engine's `add` op
so the accumulation is differentiable when `create_graph=true`.

methods.name: absorbs_phantom_gradient
methods.signature: bool absorbs_phantom_gradient(const int & grad)
methods.summary: The phantom write rule (`absorbs_phantom_write`) for this tensor's gradient slot, held by every sink a gradient lands in — a leaf's AccumulateGrad, a retained gradient, `accumulate_grad_impl` — before it stores or adds anything.

returns.description: `true` for a phantom tensor: it takes any gradient and keeps no values, so an empty slot gets a phantom of this tensor's geometry (`.grad` then reads as one) and the caller stores nothing.

raises.description: This tensor is real and `grad` a phantom — the first gradient included, which an empty slot would otherwise take as its own.

methods.name: retains_grad
methods.signature: bool retains_grad()
methods.summary: Returns whether this tensor will retain its gradient even when it is a non-leaf.
methods.extended: Mirrors the reference framework's `tensor.retain_grad()` API.

returns.description: `true` when the engine should accumulate gradients into `grad_storage` for this tensor regardless of leaf status.

methods.name: set_retain_grad
methods.signature: void set_retain_grad(bool v)
methods.summary: Toggles gradient retention for non-leaf tensors.

methods.name: leaf_hooks
methods.signature: const int & leaf_hooks()
methods.summary: A leaf's gradient hooks (`autograd/TensorHooks.h`), or null.

methods.name: mutable_leaf_hooks
methods.signature: int & mutable_leaf_hooks()
methods.summary: The leaf-hook slot itself, constructing the `AutogradMeta` on demand — for registering the first hook.

methods.name: bump_version
methods.signature: void bump_version()
methods.summary: Increments the autograd version counter.
methods.extended:
Called by every in-place op so autograd can detect mutations of
tensors that were saved for backward.  The tensor's own count moves
whether or not it has an `AutogradMeta` yet.  Having none does
not mean the tensor is outside every graph: `w * buf` saves `buf`
to differentiate with respect to `w`, though `buf` never required
grad.  When the count stayed put for such a tensor, a CPU write into
its buffer (`fill_`, `copy_`, the index writes) went unseen, and
backward computed `w`'s gradient from the values written after the
forward.  The meta lives inside the tensor (`std::optional`), so
making one here allocates nothing, and a forward that writes nothing
never makes one.

A Metal shared buffer's counter moves too, because another alias of
the same bytes may have been saved.  So does a view family's, for the
same reason.

methods.name: numel
methods.signature: int numel()
methods.summary: Returns the total number of elements (product of shape dimensions).

returns.description: `1` for a scalar (empty shape).

methods.name: nbytes
methods.signature: int nbytes()
methods.summary: Returns the total byte footprint of the tensor's logical data.
methods.extended:
Equal to `numel() * dtype_size(dtype())`; does **not** include any
extra storage capacity beyond the tensor's view.

returns.description: Logical byte size of the tensor data.

methods.name: is_contiguous
methods.signature: bool is_contiguous()
methods.summary: Predicate: does the current stride equal the row-major contiguous stride for this shape and dtype?

returns.description: `true` for canonically laid-out tensors; `false` for views that were transposed / sliced / otherwise reordered.

methods.name: is_dense
methods.signature: bool is_dense()
methods.summary: Predicate: contiguous, at the first byte of its storage, and covering all of it — the layout every backend kernel assumes when it reads a Storage from byte 0.  A contiguous view at an offset, or one smaller than its buffer, is contiguous but not dense.

methods.name: data_as_python
methods.signature: int data_as_python()
methods.summary: Returns the tensor data as a NumPy array.
methods.extended:
For CPU tensors the returned array is a zero-copy view backed by a
`py::capsule` that keeps the `TensorImpl` alive.  For
GPU tensors the data is synchronously downloaded to a temporary CPU
buffer first.

**See Also**

`to_bytes`  — NumPy-free alternative.
`tolist`    — nested Python list alternative.

returns.description: A NumPy array (one of the supported dtypes, except for `Dtype::C64` which is represented as a complex64 array).

methods.name: grad_as_python
methods.signature: int grad_as_python()
methods.summary: Returns the accumulated gradient as a NumPy array.
methods.extended: Identical download semantics to `data_as_python`.

returns.description: The gradient array, or `py::none` when no gradient has been computed yet.

methods.name: to_bytes
methods.signature: int to_bytes()
methods.summary: Returns the tensor data as a contiguous bytes blob, in row-major order.
methods.extended:
GPU tensors are downloaded to a temporary CPU buffer first.  No NumPy
dependency, by design — this path is what the serialization layer and
`__repr__` use to avoid pulling NumPy into `import lucid`.

returns.description: Row-major bytes blob of length `nbytes()`.

methods.name: from_bytes
methods.signature: int from_bytes(int data, int shape, Dtype dtype, Device device, bool requires_grad)
methods.summary: Reconstructs a `TensorImpl` from a raw bytes blob + metadata.
methods.extended:
Inverse of `to_bytes`.  When `device == Device::GPU` the
buffer is uploaded to MLX before returning.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Row-major byte payload.  Must be `shape_numel(shape) * dtype_size(dtype)` bytes long.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Target device.  GPU triggers an MLX upload.

parameters.name: requires_grad
parameters.description: Whether the reconstructed tensor tracks gradients.

returns.description: Newly constructed tensor.

methods.name: transfer_to_device
methods.signature: int transfer_to_device(Device target, bool requires_grad)
methods.summary: Cross-device copy without round-tripping through Python or NumPy.
methods.extended:
Dispatch summary:

* CPU → GPU: contiguous-snapshot the source view, then
    `gpu::upload_cpu_to_gpu` into a fresh GPU-private MLX array.
  * GPU → CPU: `gpu::download_gpu_to_cpu` into a fresh
    `CpuStorage`.
  * `SharedStorage` is handled by the separate
    `transfer_storage` API (zero-copy relabel); calling this method
    on a `SharedStorage` tensor falls back to a contiguous CPU
    snapshot path.

parameters.name: requires_grad
parameters.description: Whether the resulting tensor tracks gradients.

returns.description: New tensor on `target` with the same shape and dtype.

methods.name: tolist
methods.signature: int tolist()
methods.summary: Converts the tensor to a nested Python list (or a Python scalar for 0-d tensors).
methods.extended:
NumPy-free — mirrors `item`'s dtype dispatch but walks the full
shape.  Handles every supported dtype including `Dtype::C64`
(yields Python `complex`), so callers never need to fall back to
the NumPy bridge.  GPU tensors are downloaded to a temporary
`CpuStorage` via the `to_bytes` snapshot path; the heavy
lifting then runs against a contiguous row-major byte buffer.

returns.description: Nested `list` of Python scalars, or a single scalar when the tensor is 0-d.

methods.name: item
methods.signature: int item()
methods.summary: Extracts a single-element tensor's value as a Python scalar.
methods.extended:
GPU tensors are downloaded to CPU first.  The `Dtype::F16`
IEEE-754 binary16 → `float` conversion is performed engine-side so
the Python wrapper avoids duplicating the bit-fiddling logic from
`to_string`.

returns.description: `int` / `float` / `bool` / `complex` depending on dtype.

methods.name: to_string
methods.signature: int to_string(int precision, int threshold, int edgeitems)
methods.summary: Renders the tensor data as a human-readable string suitable for `__repr__`.
methods.extended:
The format roughly mirrors NumPy's `array2string` defaults but is
implemented entirely engine-side so neither Lucid nor its consumers
need NumPy.

parameters.name: precision
parameters.description: Significant digits for floating-point output.  Defaults to `4`.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: If `numel > threshold`, an edge-summary is rendered instead of the full data.  Defaults to `1000`.

parameters.name: edgeitems
parameters.description: How many items to keep at each edge of a truncated axis. Defaults to `3`.

returns.description: Human-readable rendering of the tensor.

methods.name: grad_to_tensor
methods.signature: int grad_to_tensor()
methods.summary: Wraps the tensor's accumulated gradient as a `TensorImpl` that reads the underlying buffer.
methods.extended:
Prefers the graph-mode `grad_impl` when present; otherwise wraps
the standard `grad` `Storage` directly.  Replaces the
older NumPy round-trip used by the Python-side `Tensor.grad`
accessor.  On the CPU the same impl comes back while it lives, and an
in-place op on it writes into the gradient (`take_storage_from`).

returns.description: Tensor view of the gradient, or `nullptr` when no gradient has been accumulated.

methods.name: sync_gpu_grad_slot
methods.signature: void sync_gpu_grad_slot(GpuStorage & slot, int next_arr)
methods.summary: Updates a GPU gradient slot's array while preserving any live `.grad` view-family handle attached to it.

methods.name: detach_gpu_grad_slot
methods.signature: int detach_gpu_grad_slot(int s)
methods.summary: Returns a GpuStorage whose array is a fresh shared_ptr without any GpuGradSlot deleter attached.

methods.name: copy_from
methods.signature: void copy_from(const TensorImpl & other)
methods.summary: Copies data from `other` into this tensor.
methods.extended:
Supports `CpuStorage`↔`CpuStorage`,
`GpuStorage`↔`GpuStorage`, and all combinations
involving `SharedStorage`.  Bumps the version counter on
success.

parameters.name: other
parameters.description: Source tensor.  Must have identical device, dtype, and shape.

raises.description: `other.device() != device()`.
`other.dtype() != dtype()`.
`other.shape() != shape()`.

methods.name: assign_from
methods.signature: void assign_from(const TensorImpl & other, const char * name)
methods.summary: An in-place assignment as a *user* means it, as opposed to `copy_from`, which is the raw buffer write every internal caller uses — an optimiser step, a `load_state_dict`, the compiled executable's ghost-grad placeholders.  Putting the graph handling into `copy_from` itself broke all of those at once, because the two want opposite things from the same function.
methods.extended:
Here it is the assignment: the values are overwritten, so the
tensor's place in the graph becomes the *source's* where there is
one — that is what routes the gradient to `z` in
`y.copy_(z)` — and ends where there is not.  A leaf that
requires grad is refused for the same reason every other in-place
op refuses one.

methods.name: zero_grad
methods.signature: void zero_grad()
methods.summary: Clears the accumulated gradient.
methods.extended:
Sets `grad` to `std::nullopt` but leaves the
`AutogradMeta` itself in place so subsequent backward passes
continue to accumulate.

methods.name: eval
methods.signature: void eval()
methods.summary: Forces evaluation of this tensor's lazy MLX computation graph.
methods.extended:
GPU tensors: calls `mlx::core::eval()` on the underlying array,
materialising the buffer.
CPU tensors: no-op (CPU storage is always materialised).
notes:
Required before any path that wants to dereference the GPU buffer
through a CPU pointer (e.g. `to_bytes`, `data_as_python`).

methods.name: write_into_shared
methods.signature: bool write_into_shared(const TensorImpl & src)
methods.summary: Writes `src`'s values into the shared buffer.  False when this tensor no longer is the buffer or `src` does not match it.

methods.name: copy_from_named
methods.signature: void copy_from_named(const TensorImpl & other, const char * name)
methods.summary: copy_from, raising and refusing in the name of the op that asked: assign_from passes its caller's (`fill_` may write an overlapping view, which a copy may not).

methods.name: gpu_member
methods.signature: bool gpu_member()
methods.summary: Whether this tensor reads a Metal view family's root.

methods.name: covers_root
methods.signature: bool covers_root()
methods.summary: Whether this tensor reads every element of its family's root, in the root's order — a reshape of it rather than a part.

methods.name: readable
methods.signature: const int & readable()
methods.summary: What reads of the values go through: a Metal member's elements, or the storage as it is (the CPU readers walk the geometry themselves).

methods.name: write_gpu_member
methods.signature: void write_gpu_member(const TensorImpl & src, const char * name, bool raw)
methods.summary: Replaces the Metal family root with `src`'s values laid into this member's elements, and bumps the version.  `raw` is copy_from's write rather than an in-place op's: no autograd refusals, and with no graph to protect it writes into a Metal shared buffer the root reads.

methods.name: gpu_grad_to_tensor
methods.signature: int gpu_grad_to_tensor(GpuStorage & gpu)

methods.name: drop_family_caches
methods.signature: void drop_family_caches()

methods.name: stride_
methods.signature: int & stride_()
methods.summary: Mutable stride accessor — returns the underlying `Stride` by reference so engine-side ops can rewrite strides in place without going through the full `set_meta` path.  Pairs with the public const `stride`.
notes:
Modifying the stride WITHOUT also touching `storage_` or `shape_`
produces an invalid TensorImpl — only call this from internal kernel
code that holds the necessary invariants.  Does NOT bump the version
counter; callers that change tensor geometry through this hook are
responsible for whatever bookkeeping autograd requires.

methods.name: dtype_field
methods.signature: Dtype & dtype_field()
methods.summary: Mutable dtype accessor — returns the underlying `Dtype` by reference. Rarely used outside engine internals; pairs with the public const `dtype`.
notes:
Changing the dtype WITHOUT also reinterpreting / reallocating
`storage_` is a footgun: the bytes on disk no longer match the
declared element type, so subsequent ops will read garbage.  Only call
from paths that have already updated storage to match the new dtype.

methods.name: device_field
methods.signature: Device & device_field()
methods.summary: Mutable device accessor — returns the underlying `Device` by reference.  Rarely used outside engine internals; pairs with the public const `device`.
notes:
Same footgun as `dtype_field`: changing the device WITHOUT also
migrating `storage_` to the new device produces a TensorImpl that
claims to live on one stream while its bytes live on another.  Only
call from paths that have already moved the storage.

members.summary: Reference-counted tensor implementation owned by every Python-level `lucid.Tensor`.
members.extended:
The C++ op layer receives and returns `TensorImplPtr`
(`shared_ptr<TensorImpl>`) directly; the Python wrapper is a thin layer
that forwards attribute access here.  `TensorImpl` extends
`std::enable_shared_from_this` so member functions can hand out
additional `shared_ptr` references to `*this` safely (e.g. when
building autograd graph nodes that capture the producing tensor).

**See Also**

`Storage`        — backing memory variant.
`TensorMeta`     — shape / stride / dtype / device bundle.
`AutogradMeta`   — autograd bookkeeping.

methods.name: numel
methods.signature: int numel()
methods.summary: Returns the total number of elements described by `shape`.
methods.extended:
Computed as the product of all dimension sizes; a 0-dim scalar
(empty `shape`) returns `1` by convention.

**Math**

$$ \mathrm{numel} = \prod_{i=0}^{N-1} \mathrm{shape}_i $$

returns.description: `shape[0] * shape[1] * ... * shape[N-1]`, or `1` for a scalar.

notes:
`shape_numel` is the one element-count rule; a second one here
cast a negative extent to `2^64 - 1` while allocation counted it
as empty.  A negative extent raises `InvalidArgument`.

methods.name: is_contiguous_for
methods.signature: bool is_contiguous_for(int elem_size)
methods.summary: Returns whether the stored stride matches row-major (C-order) contiguous layout for `elem_size`-byte elements.
methods.extended:
A tensor is C-contiguous when `stride[i] = elem_size *
prod(shape[i+1:])` for every axis `i`.  A 0-dim scalar is
contiguous by definition.

parameters.name: elem_size
parameters.description: Size in bytes of one element (e.g. `sizeof(float)` for `F32`).  Must match the `dtype` width for the result to be meaningful.

returns.description: `true` if `stride` matches C-contiguous layout for the given element size, `false` otherwise.  Returns `false` when `stride.size()` does not match `shape.size()`.

notes:
Used by `TensorImpl::is_contiguous` and by op kernels that
require contiguous input — non-contiguous tensors must be
materialised via a copy before such kernels run.

members.summary: Geometric and type description of a tensor.
members.extended:
`TensorMeta` is stored **by value** inside `TensorImpl`
(not on the heap) so that shape / dtype / device queries are a single
pointer dereference.  Views share the same `Storage` as their
base tensor but carry an independent `TensorMeta` with
potentially different shape, stride, or implicit byte offset (the
offset is encoded in `Storage`).
notes:
Equality of two `TensorMeta` instances is structural —
matching shape, stride, dtype, and device implies the two metas
describe layout-equivalent tensors (modulo storage offset).

attributes.name: stride
attributes.description: Per-dimension byte strides.  Must have `stride.size() == shape.size()` to be considered a valid contiguous layout by `is_contiguous_for`.

attributes.name: dtype
attributes.description: Element type tag.  Defaults to `Dtype::F32`.

attributes.name: device
attributes.description: Memory domain owning the underlying storage.  Defaults to `Device::CPU`.

members.summary: Autograd node for element-wise truncation toward zero: $y = \operatorname{trunc}(x)$.
members.extended:
Piecewise-constant like floor and ceil, and kept in the graph the same way,
with a zero gradient.  No backend has a trunc kernel, so the forward picks
`floor` for $x \ge 0$ and `ceil` below — on storages, so no autograd
node sits in between.  It used to be that composition over tensors, and
once floor and ceil kept the graph a `where` node landed on the path,
which refuses a second derivative: `fmod` and `frac` lost theirs.

**Math**

$$y_i = \operatorname{sgn}(x_i) \lfloor |x_i| \rfloor$$, with
`trunc(-0.0) = -0.0` and `trunc(-0.5) = -0.0`.
notes: Integer dtypes are a no-op.

members.summary: CRTP base for single-input, single-output op kernels.
members.extended:
Inherits `AutogradNode\<Derived, 1\>` (one saved input slot)
and `kernel::IKernel` so an instance can be held polymorphically
while still exposing the typed static `forward()` trampoline.

Concrete ops declare themselves as
`class FooBackward : public UnaryKernel<FooBackward>` and provide:

- `static constexpr OpSchema schema_v1` — op name + AMP policy.
  - `static cpu_kernel(a, out_shape, dtype) -> CpuStorage` and/or
    `static gpu_kernel(a, out_shape, dtype) -> GpuStorage`, **or**
    `static dispatch(IBackend&, a, out_shape, dtype) -> Storage`.
  - `Storage grad_formula(Storage grad_out)` — the local Jacobian
    product computed at backward time.
  - Optional `grad_formula_impl(grad_out, a_impl, out_impl) -> TensorImplPtr`
    for graph-mode (create_graph=True) higher-order differentiation.

Template Parameters
-------------------
Derived : class
    The concrete CRTP self-type.

**See Also**

`BinaryKernel`, `NaryKernel`, `VariadicKernel`.
`IKernel` — the abstract base above the CRTP layer.
notes:
AMP policy and dtype promotion are forwarded through
`SchemaGuard` using `Derived::schema_v1`; the effective dtype
returned drives both the input cast and the saved-input dtype.

attributes.name: kSavesInput
attributes.description: Whether `forward()` snapshots `a->storage()` into `saved_inputs_[0]` for use in `grad_formula`.  Defaults to `true`; set `false` when the gradient formula uses only the saved output (e.g. `ReLU` keyed on output sign).

attributes.name: kSavesOutput
attributes.description: Whether `forward()` additionally snapshots the output storage into `saved_output_`.  Defaults to `false`.  Set `true` for ops whose backward is cheap in terms of `y` (e.g. `Exp`, `Sigmoid`).

attributes.name: kHasGradient
attributes.description: Whether the op participates in autograd.  Defaults to `true`; set `false` for non-differentiable ops to skip all graph wiring.

members.summary: Autograd node for the Unfold (im2col) operation.
members.extended:
Slides a kernel-sized window over each spatial dimension of the input
and lays the resulting patches out as columns of a 3-D matrix:

$$
y[b,\, c \cdot \prod K + k_0 \cdot K_1 \cdots + k_{N-1},\,
  o_0 \cdot \prod O' + \cdots + o_{N-1}]
  = x[b,\, c,\, s_0 o_0 + d_0 k_0,\, \ldots].
$$

The output column count equals $\prod_i O_i$, the same value a
matching convolution would produce.  Supports $N \in \{1, 2, 3\}$
inferred from `kernel.size()`.

members.summary: Fluent precondition checker for a single tensor input.
members.extended:
Each method either evaluates one precondition and returns `*this`
(success), or throws the appropriate typed `LucidError` subclass
via `ErrorBuilder` (failure).  Chaining lets op implementations
state all of their input requirements in one compact expression at the
top of their body.

Instances cannot be constructed directly — use the static
`input` factory.  The validator holds a *reference* to the
caller's `TensorImplPtr` rather than a copy, so the chain must live no
longer than the tensor it inspects (this is the normal case when the
chain appears on a single statement at the op's entry point).

**See Also**

`Validator::Pair` : Two-tensor sibling for cross-tensor checks.
`ErrorBuilder` : Underlying throw machinery.
examples:
```
Validator::input(t, "linear.weight")
    .non_null()
    .float_only()
    .ndim(2);
```

members.extended:
Each tensor carries a monotonically increasing version counter; the saved
snapshot records the version observed at save time.  When the snapshot is
restored during backward, the engine compares the saved version against
the tensor's current version and raises `VersionMismatch` if they
differ — preventing silently incorrect gradients caused by in-place
mutation.  Mapped to `lucid._C.engine.VersionMismatch` on the Python
side.

the version counter on the underlying storage or be re-implemented as a
non-aliasing copy.  Catching `VersionMismatch` and continuing is
strongly discouraged — the gradient is no longer well-defined.

members.summary: Autograd node for reshape, squeeze, and unsqueeze.
members.extended:
Forward reinterprets the flat element buffer under a new shape.  The
backend dispatcher's reshape creates a new `Storage` alias over the same
physical buffer; no data movement occurs.  Backward reshapes the incoming
gradient back to the original input shape recorded in `input_shapes_[0]`;
because reshape is its own inverse on contiguous buffers (element ordering
is unchanged), the backward pass is simply another reshape call.

**Math**

$$ y_k = x_k \quad \text{for } k \in [0, \mathrm{numel}(x)), $$
where indices are taken in row-major flat ordering.  The mapping between
multi-dim indices changes, but the linear element ordering does not.

**Shape**

`input_shapes_[0]` — shape of the input tensor before the reshape.
`out_shape_`       — shape after the reshape (inherited from
                       `FuncOp`).  Both must have identical element
                       counts.

**See Also**

`reshape_op`, `squeeze_op`, `unsqueeze_op`,
`contiguous_op`.

parameters.name: grad_out
parameters.description: Incoming gradient, shaped according to the forward output (`out_shape_`).

returns.description: Single-element vector containing the gradient reshaped to `input_shapes_[0]`.

notes:
In graph mode `apply_for_graph` routes through `reshape_op` so the

members.name: ViewFamily
members.summary: The tensors that read one buffer, as `TensorImpl::make_view` made them.
members.extended:
Every member holds this through `shared_ptr`, so `use_count()` is how
many of them are alive.  They share one version counter — a write
through any member moves every member's `version()`, so a node that
saved one of them notices — and an in-place write to a member goes into
the buffer instead of a new storage slot, so the others see it
(`TensorImpl::write_through`).  `members` is how autograd finds
the others to re-derive from the one written; entries expire with their
tensors.

A Metal family has no shared bytes to write into — an MLX array is a
value — so it keeps the buffer's current value instead, as `root`: a
dense GpuStorage of `nbytes` bytes in any shape.  Each member reads its
elements out of the root through its own geometry, and a write through
any member replaces the root (core/GpuStrided.h).

methods.name: scatter_set_lines
methods.signature: void scatter_set_lines()
methods.summary: The overwrite scatter's loop, for `W`-byte elements and index type `I`.  It never does arithmetic on a value, so it moves bytes: one loop per element width serves every dtype of that width.  The `memcpy` of a constant `W` compiles to a single load and store.
methods.extended:
`k` ascends for every (outer, inner) line, so a position named twice
keeps the value written last, as the reference's CPU kernel does.
`j` innermost keeps the src reads and the base writes sequential.

methods.name: scatter_reduce_loop
methods.signature: int scatter_reduce_loop(const int & base, const int & indices, const int & src, const int & base_shape, const int & idx_shape, int dim, Dtype dt, const char * name, cpu::ScatterReduce reduce)
methods.summary: Generic scatter-reduce loop shared by scatter_amax / scatter_amin / scatter_prod. Every dtype at its own width but half, which widens to float32 here; see ScatterReduce.h.
methods.extended:
The index is read at its own width and checked against the axis.  This
loop read every index as int32 lanes (an int64 index of 2^32 + 1 was 1)
and wrote wherever the value pointed, so an out-of-range index wrote
past the buffer.  It also placed the index's elements by the base's
strides, so an index narrower than the base off `dim` read past the
index and src and took the process down with SIGBUS.
`axis_scatter_walk` places them now, as it does for scatter_add and
scatter_set.

methods.summary: Overwrite scatter: a copy of `base` with `out[..., idx[..., k, ...], ...] = src[..., k, ...]` along `dim`.
methods.extended:
Every dtype, by element width.  It shared the reduce loop above, which
instantiates f32 and f64 only, so `index_copy` of a bool, integer,
half or complex tensor refused (CHA-27) — and `x[key] = v` had been
routed around it through an additive delta that could not express an
overwrite at all (CHA-158).  The index may be shorter than `base` on
every axis but `dim`, as for `scatter_add`; a repeated index keeps
the value written last.

methods.name: unpack_eig
methods.signature: void unpack_eig()
methods.summary: Unpack one matrix's worth of LAPACK `?geev` output into complex.
methods.extended:
`?geev` reports a real matrix's spectrum in two real arrays,
`wr` and `wi`, and its eigenvectors in a single real `VR`
where a conjugate pair occupies two adjacent columns.  Reading only
`wr` and copying `VR` verbatim is what this backend used to do,
and for a matrix with any complex eigenvalue that is not a lossy
answer but a wrong one: the pair a \u00b1 bi came back as a, a — two
equal reals where there were two conjugate numbers — with nothing
to say the imaginary halves had been dropped.

A real matrix having complex eigenvalues is the ordinary case, not
a corner one.  Any rotation has them; so does every companion
matrix of a polynomial with complex roots.  It went unnoticed
because a symmetric or triangular test matrix has a real spectrum,
and those are what test suites reach for.

The packing, from `?geev`'s documentation: if `wi[j]` is zero,
eigenvector j is column j of `VR`.  Otherwise j and j+1 are a
conjugate pair with `wi[j] > 0`, and

v[j]   = VR[:, j] + i * VR[:, j + 1]
    v[j+1] = VR[:, j] - i * VR[:, j + 1]

`vr` arrives row-major (the LAPACK wrapper transposes on the way
out), so eigenvector j is still column j, read with stride n.

methods.extended:
Generic Cartesian-product cast over the supported scalar dtypes.  Earlier
versions of this file hand-spelled every supported (src, dst) pair, which
left holes (notably `Bool -> I64`) that surfaced during the 3.0.2 +
followup smoke runs — bool reductions need to promote through I64 first
and that promotion was silently NotImplementedError.  The dispatch below
covers every pair among {F16, F32, F64, I8, I16, I32, I64, Bool}.  C64
and BF16 are handled outside the table, through float32, because their
host representation isn't a simple `static_cast`-able scalar (F16 uses the IEEE half decoder from
`item()` indirectly via the F32 path — handled with a small helper).

methods.signature: void ctnd_im2col(const float * src, float * cols, int C, const int * O, const int * K, const int * S, const int * stride, const int * pad, const int * dil, int N)
methods.summary: `im2col` / `col2im` / GEMM shims for the transposed convolution.
methods.extended:
The transposed conv is the data gradient of a forward convolution, so
the roles are crossed relative to the forward path: the *output*
extent `O` plays the forward conv's input length and the *input*
extent `S` plays its output length.  That is why `O` is passed
where the primitives name their argument `L` / `H` / `D`.

The `dilation` argument used to be hardcoded to `1` here, which
is what confined the whole op to `dilation == 1`; the underlying
primitives have always accepted it.

members.summary: CPU (Apple Accelerate-backed) concrete `IBackend`.
members.extended:
Every public method satisfies the `IBackend` contract; the
private section holds low-level type-dispatch helpers (`unary_op`,
`binary_op`, `reduce_axes`) plus per-op compute routines that
delegate to the Accelerate helpers in `Blas.h`,
`Lapack.h`, `Norm.h`, `Pool.h`, `Reduce.h`,
`Vdsp.h`, and `Vforce.h`.

**See Also**

`IBackend` — abstract base.
`GpuBackend` — MLX/Metal counterpart.
`Dispatcher` — owns the singleton instance.
notes:
Marked `final` — there is exactly one CPU backend at runtime,
installed by `CpuBackendRegistrar` at static-init time.

members.name: AxisScatterWalk
members.summary: Where an axis scatter's writes land in `base`.
members.extended:
The walk is over the *index's* extents, which may be shorter than
base's on any axis but `dim` (src arrives cut to the index's shape),
so each outer (before `dim`) and inner (after) coordinate of the
index is placed by base's strides.  When the shapes agree this is
`(o * base_dim + tgt) * inner + j` exactly.  Index and src are dense
in the index's shape: element `(o, k, j)` is at
`(o * idx_dim + k) * inner + j`.

members.name: Dispatcher

methods.name: for_device
methods.signature: IBackend & for_device(Device d)
methods.summary: Returns the backend registered for device `d`.
methods.extended:
The returned reference is non-owning and remains valid for the
entire process lifetime; callers must not delete it.

**See Also**

`register_backend` — installer counterpart.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Device tag selecting which backend to return (CPU or GPU).

returns.description: Reference to the singleton backend instance for `d`.

notes:
Behaviour is undefined if no backend has been registered for `d`
— `register_backend` must have been called for that device
before any tensor compute occurs.  `noexcept`; safe to call
concurrently after initialisation.

While `PhantomMode` is on for the calling thread, the answer is
the phantom backend for `d` instead, which computes nothing — every
op on that thread then dispatches with the shape it already computed
and gets a phantom storage back.

methods.name: register_backend
methods.signature: void register_backend(Device d, int be)
methods.summary: Registers (or replaces) the backend for device `d`.
methods.extended:
Transfers ownership of `be` into the dispatcher.  Any backend
previously stored at that slot is destroyed.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Device tag identifying which slot to populate.

parameters.name: be
parameters.description: Owning pointer to the concrete backend instance to install.

notes:
Called exactly once per `Device` during process
initialisation (typically from `CpuBackend::register_self`
and `GpuBackend::register_self`, invoked by
`BackendInit.cpp`).  Not thread-safe — must complete before any
worker threads start issuing `for_device` calls.

methods.name: phantom_backend
methods.signature: IBackend & phantom_backend(Device d)
methods.summary: The `PhantomBackend` for `d` — one per device, a static inside the function.  Defined in `BackendInit.cpp`, the one translation unit that builds the backends, so the generated class is compiled once rather than in every op that dispatches.

methods.name: instance
methods.signature: Dispatcher & instance()
methods.summary: Returns the Meyers-singleton dispatcher instance.
methods.extended:
Constructed on first call and destroyed at program exit per the
standard C++11 magic-statics guarantee.

returns.description: The process-wide dispatcher.

members.summary: Routes compute operations to the backend registered for a given Device.
members.extended:
Holds one `IBackend` slot per `Device` variant (currently
CPU and GPU).  `register_backend` transfers ownership via
`std::unique_ptr`; `for_device` returns a non-owning reference
valid for the lifetime of the process.  Every higher-level op in the
Lucid engine fetches its backend through this class — the dispatcher is
the single seam between device-agnostic op code and device-specific
compute libraries.

**See Also**

`IBackend` — abstract per-device interface.
`CpuBackend::register_self` — installs the CPU backend.
`GpuBackend::register_self` — installs the GPU backend.
notes:
Thread safety: `register_backend` is called exactly once per
device at process startup, before any worker threads exist.  After
that, `for_device` is read-only and safe to call concurrently
from any thread.

The internal storage is a fixed-size `std::array` indexed by the
`Device` enum value; `kNumDevices` must match the number of
`Device` variants (currently `CPU=0`, `GPU=1`).

methods.signature: ::mlx::core::array poison_after_nan(const ::mlx::core::array & input, const ::mlx::core::array & scanned, int axis)
methods.summary: Once a NaN appears in the scan it is the running extreme, and every later element inherits it — the same rule `max` follows.  MLX's cumulative scans skip it instead, so the CPU (fixed to propagate) and Metal disagreed from the NaN onwards.
methods.extended:
MLX has no flag for it, so it is composed: a running max over the NaN
mask says "a NaN has been seen at or before here", and those
positions are overwritten.
