methods.name: scatter_add
methods.signature: int scatter_add(const int & base, const int & indices, const int & src, const int & base_shape, const int & idx_shape, int dim, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: Scatter-add: `base[indices] += src` (out-of-place), along `dim`:   out[..., idx[..., j, ...], ...] += src[..., j, ...]
methods.extended:
`mlx::core::scatter_add_axis` is that primitive exactly.  MLX's
multi-axis `scatter_add` (np.add.at flavour: one index array per
axis) is a different operation and tripped its own "Number of index
arrays does not match number of axes" guard.  An out-of-range index
drops its update (policy B, `gpu_axis_index`).

methods.name: scatter_set
methods.signature: int scatter_set(const int & base, const int & indices, const int & src, const int & base_shape, const int & idx_shape, int dim, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: Axis-scatter overwrite — out[..., idx[..., j, ...], ...] = src[..., j, ...] along dim.  `mlx::core::put_along_axis` is the exact set-mode analogue of `scatter_add_axis` (single kernel); `x[key] = v`, `scatter` and `index_copy` route through it.  A position named twice takes one of the values aimed at it, which one unspecified unless deterministic mode is enabled (`put_along_axis_last_write_wins`, last write wins).
methods.extended:
An out-of-range index drops its write (policy B, `gpu_axis_index`).
It is aimed at a one-wide sink slab past the end of `dim` that is cut
off again (`gpu_sink_index`), because no in-range position can take
a write and stay as it was.

MLX scatters no 8-byte element on Metal: int64 and complex64 both
report "[ScatterAxis::eval_gpu] Does not support".  Writing each as
two uint32 halves would be exact for distinct indices, but two writers
racing for one position can land one's low half beside the other's
high half — a value nobody wrote.  So those two go through the CPU,
sink slab and all.

methods.name: scatter_via_cpu
methods.signature: int scatter_via_cpu()
methods.summary: MLX's Metal scatter has no int64 kernel (nor complex64 — see scatter_set).
methods.extended:
`[ScatterAxis::eval_gpu] Does not support int64` — the *values*,
not the indices, which it takes at either width.  There is no exact
way around it on-device: float32 loses everything above 2^24, and
splitting the word into two int32 halves works for a set but not
for an add, where the carry between halves is exactly what is lost.

So int64 scatter runs on the CPU and comes back.  It is a real cost
and it is stated here rather than hidden: the alternative was
`lucid.scatter` and `index_copy` raising on Metal for a dtype
the CPU handles, which is the device-dependent behaviour this
backend pair exists to avoid.  Same shape as the LAPACK pivot
round-trips further up this file.

methods.name: axis_scatter_via_multiaxis
methods.signature: int axis_scatter_via_multiaxis()
methods.summary: MLX's `scatter_{max,min,prod}` have no axis-only variant the way `scatter_add` has `scatter_add_axis`.  So the axis scatter `a[..., idx[i,j,...], ...] op= src[i,j,...]` along `dim` uses the multi-axis form with K = ndim: one coordinate array per axis.  For every axis but `dim` the coordinate is `arange(idx_shape[a])` reshaped to (1..N..1).  For `dim` it is the index, made safe by `gpu_axis_index`.  Updates then have the index's shape, which meets MLX's "updates.ndim == K + (ndim - K)" invariant.
methods.extended:
An out-of-range index drops its update (policy B): the update becomes
the identity of `op`.

methods.signature: int layer_norm_forward(const int & x, const int & gamma, const int & beta, int outer, int normalized_size, double eps, const int & x_shape, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: ── Normalisation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── LayerNorm forward via MLX's fused `fast::layer_norm` kernel.
methods.extended:
**Math**

$$\mu = \mathbb{E}[x], \quad \mathrm{rstd} = (\operatorname{Var}[x] + \varepsilon)^{-1/2}$$
$$y = \gamma \, (x - \mu) \, \mathrm{rstd} + \beta$$
reducing along the trailing axis of size `normalized_size`.

returns.description: `{y, saved_mean, saved_rstd}` — the activation plus saved stats needed by `layer_norm_backward`.

notes:
Replaces the 7-op MLX chain (mean → subtract → square → mean →
add+rsqrt → multiply → multiply+add) with one fused kernel.
Mac Studio Llama-scale forward: 2.4 ms → ~0.6 ms.

methods.summary: Matrix / vector norm.  Routed to MLX's CPU linalg stream per H3.
methods.extended:
**Math**

axis pair this is the Frobenius / spectral norm depending on

notes:

methods.name: linalg_cholesky
methods.signature: int linalg_cholesky(const int & a, const int &, bool upper, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: Cholesky factorisation $A = L L^T$ (or $U^T U$ if `upper`), on MLX's CPU linalg stream.
methods.extended:
MLX reports no failure.  Its *lower* factor keeps LAPACK's failed
pivot — the first diagonal entry that is not positive, or is NaN, at
the step `potrf` stopped — so `info` is read there.  Its upper
factor does not: `[[1, 2], [2, 1]]` came back `[[1, 2], [0, 1]]`
(LCD-206).  So `U` of `A` is `L` of `A^T`, transposed: the
same triangle read, one check for both.

methods.name: linalg_inv
methods.signature: int linalg_inv(const int & a, const int &, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: Dense matrix inverse $A^{-1}$ via the MLX CPU linalg stream.
methods.extended:
Built from MLX's LU factors rather than `linalg::inv`, which throws
from the CPU stream's worker thread on a singular matrix and so
aborts the process — see `gpu_lu_inverse`.  A singular input raises
the same `LinAlgError` the CPU stream does.

methods.name: linalg_solve
methods.signature: int linalg_solve(const int & a, const int & b, const int & a_shape, const int & b_shape, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: Solve the linear system $A x = b$ for `x`.  CPU linalg stream.
methods.extended:
`x = A^{-1} b` with the inverse from `gpu_lu_inverse`:
`linalg::solve` inverts the triangular factors with the same
throwing routine, so a singular `A` aborted the process here too.
MLX's own solve is a product with explicit triangular inverses, so
this is the same arithmetic in a different order, not a weaker one.

methods.name: nn_fold
methods.signature: int nn_fold(const int & x, const int & x_shape, const int & out_shape, const int & kernel_size, const int & stride, const int & padding, const int & dilation, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: fold (col2im) — Metal-native via `scatter_add_axis`.
methods.extended:
Algorithm: precompute on CPU a length-(kH*kW*L) table of flat output
positions (oh*outW + ow) for every (ki, kj, l_idx) triple plus a
matching validity mask.  Upload both as small MLX arrays.  Then a
single `scatter_add_axis` call accumulates the (N, C, kH*kW, L)
input slices into the (N, C, outH*outW) output buffer along axis 2.
Invalid (out-of-bounds) source elements are zeroed via the mask, so
they scatter +0 to position 0 and have no effect on the result.
`nn.Fold` — reverse of `nn.Unfold`: scatters unfolded patches back into a feature map.
notes:
Built atop MLX's `scatter_add` because patches may overlap and
must accumulate.

**Math**

$$y_{n,c_o,p_1,\ldots,p_N} = b_{c_o} + \sum_{c_i} \sum_{\Delta} W_{c_o,c_i,\Delta} \, x_{n,c_i,p_1 s_1 + \Delta_1,\ldots}$$

input + weight NCHW → NHWC, dispatches `mlx::core::conv1d` /

methods.name: gpu_lu_inverse
methods.signature: ::mlx::core::array gpu_lu_inverse(const ::mlx::core::array & a, const char * op)
methods.summary: $A^{-1}$ for a batch of square matrices, from MLX's LU factors.
methods.extended:
`linalg::lu` reports a zero pivot by leaving it in `U` rather than
by throwing, so the pivots are read back and a singular matrix raises
here — the CPU stream's `LinAlgError`, `info` being the 1-based
index of the first zero pivot, as LAPACK numbers it.  Only then are
the factors inverted, and `tri_inv` fails on nothing but an exactly
zero diagonal: `U`'s was just checked, `L`'s is all ones.  (A
NaN pivot is not zero; it propagates into a NaN inverse, which is
what LAPACK's own `getri` returns for it.)

MLX's `lu` gives `A = L[P] U` with `P` a row-index vector, so
$A^{-1} = U^{-1} L^{-1} P^T$, whose column `j` is column `P[j]`
of $U^{-1} L^{-1}$.

methods.name: mlx_unary
methods.signature: int mlx_unary()
methods.summary: Applies a unary MLX operation fn to the underlying array and wraps the result in a new GpuStorage.
methods.extended:
No mlx::core::contiguous() call here: element-wise MLX ops (exp, sin,
abs, relu, …) always write to a freshly allocated C-contiguous Metal
buffer regardless of the input strides.  Adding contiguous() would insert
a redundant lazy graph node that MLX must inspect and discard at eval
time, adding ~150 µs of overhead per call on 10M-element float32 arrays.

If an op genuinely needs the output to be contiguous (e.g. a view op),
call mlx_unary_contiguous() instead or wrap explicitly.

methods.name: mlx_unary_contiguous
methods.signature: int mlx_unary_contiguous()
methods.summary: Variant of mlx_unary that forces C-contiguous output.  Use only for ops that may produce strided/non-contiguous results (e.g. view ops).

methods.name: mlx_unary_fused
methods.signature: int mlx_unary_fused()
methods.summary: Fuse a multi-op element-wise UNARY composite into a single Metal kernel via mlx::core::compile (shapeless → traced once on first call, then the fused kernel is reused for every shape and dtype).  MLX eager does NOT fuse element-wise chains (that is what compile is for), so a composite such as gelu (~9 primitives) otherwise pays one kernel launch + a DRAM round-trip PER primitive.  Fusing collapses it to one pass — e.g. gelu_exact 1.71 ms -> 0.48 ms on (32,128,3072) F32 (faster than the reference framework), bit-exact (maxdiff <= 2.4e-7; F16/BF16 exact).
methods.extended:
Use ONLY for genuine multi-op composites; single-primitive ops
(relu/sigmoid/exp) gain nothing.  `fn` MUST be capture-less — derive any
dtype-specific constant from the input's dtype (`x.dtype()`), never from
a captured `Dtype` (the compile overload needs a function-pointer-
convertible lambda).  The compiled function is a function-local static, so
it is built once per distinct `Fn` type and reused thereafter.

methods.signature: int mlx_binary_fused()
methods.summary: Binary counterpart of `mlx_unary_fused` — for two-input element-wise composites (e.g. activation backward passes consuming the input and the incoming gradient).  Same caching, same capture-less requirement.

methods.name: mlx_binary
methods.signature: int mlx_binary()
methods.summary: Applies a binary MLX operation fn to two GpuStorage arrays.  Shape is ignored because MLX handles broadcasting internally.
methods.extended:
Same rationale as mlx_unary: binary element-wise ops always produce
C-contiguous output in MLX, so contiguous() is not needed here.

members.summary: Concrete GPU backend routing every Lucid op through Apple's MLX library.
members.extended:
Inherits `IBackend` and overrides each per-op virtual to call
the matching `mlx::core::*` primitive (broadcast, matmul, reduce,
activations, …).  Results are MLX lazy arrays — `mx::eval()` is
invoked when the engine needs the concrete buffer (e.g. for
`MetalKernelRunner` or `download_gpu_to_cpu`).  Stream
tagging uses `Dispatcher`'s default GPU stream unless an op
requests another (linalg ops dispatch to a CPU MLX stream per the
H3 carve-out, since MLX's eigh / svd / qr run on CPU).

**See Also**

`CpuBackend` — Accelerate-backed sibling.
`MlxBridge` — Storage ↔ mlx::core::array conversion.
`GpuBackendRegistrar` — static-init registration.
examples: Construction is automatic via static registration::
notes:
- CPU and GPU backends are static singletons registered with the
  `Dispatcher` at process start (see `GpuBackendRegistrar`).
- All Storage values passed in MUST hold `GpuStorage` — the
  Dispatcher guarantees this by routing Device::GPU tensors here.
- MLX uses lazy evaluation; operations build a graph but defer
  execution until `eval()` or a CPU read forces it.
- `Dtype::F64` is unsupported on the GPU (Metal limitation); callers
  must cast to F32 or keep the tensor on the CPU.
- Convolutions internally permute NCHW ↔ NHWC because MLX expects
  channels-last; see `gpu_nchw_to_nhwc_perm` family of helpers.

members.name: AlignedConv
members.summary: Convolution operands with their channels aligned, so MLX never pads them.
members.extended:
MLX pads unaligned channels up to a multiple of 16 inside the Metal
convolution — 2-D from 0.32.1 (`pad_in_channels_conv_2D_gpu`), 3-D in
every release (`pad_and_slice_conv_3D_gpu`) — and fills the padding
from a zero scalar it does not keep alive: the kernel reads it on the GPU
after the function that made it has freed it.  When the allocator hands
that buffer to another array first — any scalar written while the work is
still queued, which `async_eval` makes routine — the padded channels
take its value instead of zero and the convolution comes out wrong, whole
layers off and some NaN (a ResNet on MNIST: 4 of 16 Metal training
forwards on MLX 0.32.1).  Padding here, as a graph op, gives the same zero
channels from buffers MLX tracks, and MLX then runs the kernel it padded
for.  Both operands get the same extra channels, all zero, so every added
product is zero and the result is exact.

The conditions mirror MLX's own: groups == 1 and no input dilation, then
for 2-D a stride-1 kernel of area >= 9 whose input channels are above 4
and unaligned while its output channels are aligned; for 3-D any
unaligned channels, output channels included (sliced off after).

methods.name: add
methods.signature: int add(const int & a, const int & b, const int & shape, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: Elementwise arithmetic on two broadcast-prepared operands.
methods.extended:
Each of the five primitives below computes `out[i] = a[i] op b[i]`
for every element, with both `a` and `b` already broadcast (by
the caller) to the common output `shape`.

**Math**

$$\mathrm{out}[i] = \begin{cases}
  a[i] + b[i] & \text{add} \\
  a[i] - b[i] & \text{sub} \\
  a[i] \cdot b[i] & \text{mul} \\
  a[i] / b[i] & \text{div} \\
  a[i]^{b[i]} & \text{pow}
\end{cases}$$

parameters.name: dt
parameters.description: Element dtype (common to `a`, `b`, and the result).

returns.description: Newly-allocated output buffer of the same shape and dtype.

  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial y}

methods.name: batch_norm_forward
methods.signature: int batch_norm_forward(const int & x, const int & gamma, const int & beta, int batch, int channels, int spatial, int ndim, double eps, const int & x_shape, Dtype dt)
methods.summary: BatchNorm training forward.  ndim distinguishes 1-D, 2-D, and 3-D spatial tensors.  Returns [output, saved_mean, saved_rstd, saved_xnorm].  The 4th element (xnorm = (x - mean) * rstd) is the normalised input that backward needs; the MLX forward path already materialises it as a lazy intermediate, so exposing it costs nothing at forward time and saves a recomputation at backward time.  Backends without a meaningful xnorm intermediate (e.g. the MPSGraph dispatch) may return an empty Storage for slot 3 — the backward will then fall back to recomputing.

methods.name: batch_norm_backward
methods.signature: int batch_norm_backward(const int & x, const int & gamma, const int & saved_mean, const int & saved_rstd, const int & saved_xnorm, const int & grad, int batch, int channels, int spatial, int ndim, const int & x_shape, Dtype dt, double eps)
methods.summary: BatchNorm backward; returns [grad_x, grad_gamma, grad_beta]. `eps` matches the forward's epsilon — GPU backend needs it to reconstruct variance from saved_rstd (var = 1/rstd^2 - eps) for the MPSGraph normalizationGradient* path.  CPU backend may ignore.
methods.extended:
3.4+ Phase A.4: `saved_xnorm` optionally carries the forward's
normalised input `(x - mean) * rstd` as a full-size tensor (same
shape as `x`).  When present (i.e. non-empty Storage) the MLX-path
backward consumes it directly and skips two element-wise ops per
BN backward (centered = x - mean; xnorm = centered * rstd).  Passing
an empty Storage triggers the prior recomputation path — required
for the MPSGraph dispatch, which has its own xnorm management.

methods.summary: Scaled dot-product attention forward.  Returns [output, saved_weights] where saved_weights holds the post-softmax attention scores for backward. is_causal=true applies a lower-triangular mask to prevent attending to future tokens without materialising the full mask tensor. `need_weights` selects the return contract: `false` uses the memory-efficient fused kernel and returns a placeholder weights slot; `true` materializes the dense softmax weight matrix (O(T²)) for callers that inspect it. `attn_mask` / `mask_dtype` / `is_causal` mirror `sdpa_forward` so a

the exact masked attention.  `attn_mask` is `nullptr` when absent; a
`Bool` `mask_dtype` marks a keep-mask, any other dtype an additive mask.

methods.summary: Gradient of each sample's CTC loss with respect to log_probs, (T, N, C). grad_out: (N,) upstream gradient of every per-sample loss. methods.summary: Draw a {0,1} Bernoulli keep-mask at rate `keep_prob` directly on-device, deterministically seeded by `key_seed` (pulled from the framework Generator so the mask is reproducible from the global seed).  Returned as `dt`-typed {0,1} values; the inverted-dropout `1/keep_prob` scaling is applied by the caller.  Default: not implemented — the CPU path uses the per-element Generator loop in `bernoulli_mask_storage_shape`.  The GPU backend overrides this to skip that scalar CPU loop + host->device upload, which otherwise dominates Dropout cost (~19 ms for a single (32,128,768) mask vs <1 ms on-device).

members.summary: Abstract compute backend interface.
members.extended:
One concrete `IBackend` exists per `Device` slot (CPU,
GPU); `Dispatcher` holds them and routes every op based on the
tensor's device tag.  Implementations dispatch the actual math to
their device-native library — Apple Accelerate (vDSP / vForce / BLAS
/ LAPACK) for CPU, MLX for GPU.

**See Also**

`CpuBackend` — Accelerate-backed concrete CPU.
`GpuBackend` — MLX-backed concrete GPU.
`Dispatcher` — selects which to use.
notes:
**Ownership.**  Each concrete backend is created once and stored
inside the `Dispatcher` singleton via `std::unique_ptr`; the
lifetime of every `IBackend` therefore equals the lifetime of
the process.

**Thread safety.**  Methods are *thread-compatible* but not internally
synchronised: the engine never calls into the same backend from
multiple threads simultaneously on the same op, though distinct ops
on distinct tensors may overlap.  Callers that share a backend across
threads must provide their own serialisation, or rely on the
underlying framework (e.g. MLX's own thread-safety guarantees).

**Design rationale.**  All methods take `Storage` by
const-reference and return a new `Storage`; no in-place
mutation is exposed at this layer.  Concrete implementations choose
the most efficient internal representation — `CpuStorage` (Apple
aligned host buffer) for CPU, `GpuStorage` (`mlx::core::array`)
for GPU.

members.name: ConvNdOpts
members.summary: Compact parameter bag for N-D standard convolution.
members.extended:
Used by `IBackend::conv_nd_forward` and
`conv_nd_backward` for `N` in `{1, 2, 3}`.  The
fixed-size arrays are indexed `0..N-1`; any unused trailing
entries are ignored by the implementation.

attributes.name: N
attributes.description: Number of spatial dimensions (1, 2, or 3).

attributes.name: groups
attributes.description: Channel grouping factor; `1` means standard convolution and `Cin` means depthwise.

attributes.name: stride, pad, dilation
attributes.description: Per-spatial-dimension geometry (only the first `N` entries are meaningful).

members.name: ConvTransposeNdOpts
members.summary: Compact parameter bag for N-D transposed convolution.
members.extended:
Mirrors `ConvNdOpts` and adds `opad`.  A transposed
convolution *is* the data gradient of a forward convolution, so
`stride` / `pad` / `dilation` / `groups` describe that
forward convolution — the one whose input this op reconstructs —
and `opad` picks one output extent out of the `stride`
candidates an integer-dividing stride leaves ambiguous.

attributes.name: N
attributes.description: Number of spatial dimensions (1, 2, or 3).

attributes.name: groups
attributes.description: Channel grouping factor; `1` is the dense case and `Cin` is depthwise.  Unlike `ConvNdOpts`, the divided axis of the weight is the *second* one: `(Cin, Cout / groups, K...)`.

attributes.name: stride, pad, dilation, opad
attributes.description: Per-spatial-dimension geometry (only the first `N` entries are meaningful).

members.name: LstmOpts
members.summary: Parameter bag for LSTM operations.
members.extended:
Used by `lstm_forward`, `lstm_forward_train`, and
`lstm_backward`.  `weights` is supplied separately as
`std::vector<Storage>` in the order
`[W_ih, W_hh, b_ih, b_hh]` per layer; bidirectional layers
double the count (forward block followed by reverse block).

When `proj_size > 0` (the projected-LSTM / LSTMP variant) an
additional weight tensor `W_hr` of shape `(proj_size,
hidden_size)` is appended per layer so the order becomes
`[W_ih, W_hh, b_ih, b_hh, W_hr]`.  The recurrent weight
`W_hh` then has its second axis sized `proj_size` instead of
`hidden_size` because the projected hidden state feeds the
next time step.  The cell state `c_n` keeps shape
`hidden_size` regardless.

attributes.name: input_size, hidden_size
attributes.description: Input feature size and recurrent hidden size.

attributes.name: num_layers
attributes.description: Number of stacked LSTM layers.

attributes.name: seq_len, batch_size
attributes.description: Time and batch dimensions of the input sequence.

attributes.name: batch_first
attributes.description: If `true` the input is laid out as `(batch, seq, input)`; otherwise `(seq, batch, input)`.

attributes.name: bidirectional
attributes.description: Whether to run a reverse-direction stack alongside the forward.

attributes.name: has_bias
attributes.description: Whether the per-gate bias terms are present.

attributes.name: proj_size
attributes.description: `0` ⇒ standard LSTM; `> 0` ⇒ projected (LSTMP) variant.

members.name: PoolOpts
members.summary: Compact parameter bag for N-D pooling.
members.extended:
Used by `max_pool_nd_forward`, `avg_pool_nd_forward`,
and their backward counterparts for `N` in `{1, 2, 3}`.

attributes.name: K
attributes.description: Kernel size per spatial dimension.

attributes.name: stride
attributes.description: Stride per spatial dimension.

attributes.name: pad
attributes.description: Symmetric (both-sides) padding per spatial dimension.

attributes.name: N
attributes.description: Number of spatial dimensions actually used.

members.name: MatmulOpts
members.summary: Parameter bag for a single matrix-multiplication call.
members.extended:
Carries the logical shape and transposition flags for one `a @ b`
product.  Dimensions are interpreted in *logical* (not transposed)
order so the result is always $(M \times K) \cdot (K \times N) = (M
\times N)$ regardless of the `transA` / `transB` flags.

**See Also**

`IBackend::matmul` — consumes this struct.

attributes.name: transA
attributes.description: If `true` the dispatched kernel treats the left operand as transposed before contraction.

attributes.name: M
attributes.description: Number of rows of the (post-transpose) left operand.

attributes.name: K
attributes.description: Contracted inner dimension.

attributes.name: N
attributes.description: Number of columns of the (post-transpose) right operand.

attributes.name: batch
attributes.description: Number of independent matmuls stacked along the leading axis. `batch == 1` is the standard 2-D case; `batch > 1` indicates a batched matmul where the same A/B strides repeat `batch` times.

members.summary: Backward-side context container.
members.extended:
Holds the active `MPSGraph` (shared with the forward
`BuilderContext`), a back-reference to the forward context
for saved-input lookups, and the trace-id → gradient-tensor map.
Two id namespaces are kept disjoint: the forward context owns
`tid → MPSGraphTensor*` (forward activations); this container
owns `tid → MPSGraphTensor*` for backward gradients keyed on the
*same* trace id.  VJPs read forward activations via `forward`

methods.name: compute_grads
methods.signature: bool compute_grads(TensorId loss_id, const int & param_ids, int & out_grads, int * error_msg, int * absent)
methods.summary: Compute gradients of `param_ids` w.r.t. `loss_id`.
methods.extended:
On success: `out_grads` is resized to `param_ids.size()` and
entry `i` holds the `MPSGraphTensor*` (as `void*`) gradient
of the loss w.r.t. `param_ids[i]`.  Returns `true`.

On failure: returns `false` and writes a diagnostic to
`*error_msg` (if non-null).  Common reasons:
  * VJP coverage gap — no emitter registered for an op that lies
    on the gradient path.
  * Forward binding missing for a saved-input id.
  * VJP emitter itself signalled per-call failure.

`absent`, when given, accepts a parameter the loss does not
depend on: its gradient comes back as zeros and its slot is marked
`true` — eager leaves such a gradient `None`, and the caller
does the same.  Without it the parameter is an error.

members.summary: Reverse-mode walker.  Owns the BackwardContext and drives the per-op VJP dispatch.
members.extended:

lambda at the integration sites in `MpsBuilder.mm`; runs once
per compile.  No state survives the compile call.

methods.name: stash_saved
methods.signature: void stash_saved(TensorId out_id, const int & name, void * tensor)
methods.summary: Saved-state side-table.
methods.extended:
Used by ops whose backward needs an intermediate tensor computed
during forward emission that ISN'T derivable from the inputs +
attrs alone — most notably the RNG mask of training-mode
dropout (the same random tensor must be referenced by both
forward and backward subgraphs; recomputing would draw fresh
random values).  The forward emitter stashes the tensor via
`stash_saved(out_id, name, t)`; the VJP emitter retrieves it
via `resolve_saved(out_id, name)` and ties its backward
subgraph to the same MPSGraph node — MPSGraph evaluates each
node exactly once per dispatch, so the value is shared.

Keyed on the forward op's primary output id + a short
op-defined slot name ("mask", "y", "rstd", …).  `nullptr`
return signals "no slot found" — VJP must handle that fallback
(typically by recomputing or returning false).

Forward emitters may also record compile-time facts about a value
for later forward emitters to read (e.g. the ±0 splat marks in
_SignedZero.h); a slot name is shared by every op on that id, so a
non-VJP slot carries its owner's prefix.

methods.name: operator==
methods.signature: bool operator==(const FeedSig & other)

members.summary: Cache key — the structural signature of a `TraceGraph`.
members.extended:
Two traces share an executable iff every field below matches.  The
input *values* are not part of the key; only the per-op output meta
influences the compiled graph (because MPSGraph placeholders are
shape-static in Phase 1.2 and Phase 1.6 will introduce a separate
`dynamic` key variant).

attributes.name: op_names
attributes.description: Op-name sequence in dispatch order.  Compared element-wise.

attributes.name: op_inputs
attributes.description: Per-op input wiring: every tensor id renumbered by first appearance across the walk, so the numbers depend only on how the graph is connected and not on the ids a particular trace drew.  `a * b` fed one tensor twice reads `{0, 0}`, fed two tensors `{0, 1}`. Without this both hashed alike and one caller ran the other's executable — one feed bound where two were passed.

attributes.name: output_shapes
attributes.description: Per-op single-output shape.  Phase 1.2 supports one output per node; Phase 1.3+ may append entries for multi-output ops.

attributes.name: output_dtypes
attributes.description: Per-op single-output dtype.

attributes.name: op_attrs
attributes.description: Per-op attribute map, serialised in sorted-key order so the hash is deterministic.  Required for emitter-divergent attributes that don't show up in shapes (e.g. `dropout`'s `training` / `p`, `softmax`'s `axis`).  Without this two traces with identical structure but different attributes would collide on the same cache entry and one caller would silently receive the other's executable.

attributes.name: feeds
attributes.description: Shape + dtype of every external feed (user input or parameter), ordered by the same first-appearance numbering as `op_inputs`. The executable's placeholders are typed and shaped by its feeds and `run_executable` refuses a mismatch, so two traces whose ops agree but whose inputs do not must not share an entry.  Without this, `isnan(x) + 1` traced on float32 and then on int64 — every op output the same shape and dtype — hit the float executable and raised "feed slot 0 expects dtype float32, got int64".

attributes.name: outputs
attributes.description: The tensors the caller asked for, in order and in the same numbering. The graph alone does not say which of its values are returned: two callables tracing `(t + 1, t * 2)` and `(t * 2, t + 1)` build the same ops, and without this the second ran the first's executable and got its outputs in the first's order — as `topk(t)[0]` got the indices of an earlier `topk(t)[1]`.

attributes.name: device
attributes.description: Device on which the executable was compiled (all ops in a trace must agree on one device — Phase 1.2 builder enforces this).

members.name: GraphAxisIndex
members.summary: An index that is safe to hand to an MPSGraph gather or scatter.  Both nil when the index cannot be checked (not an integer, or the axis length is not known when the graph is built), and the emitter declines to eager then.

members.summary: A class-index target (`nll_loss`, `cross_entropy_loss`) checked against `classes` classes, one per sample.  Eager raises IndexError for a target that is neither a class nor `ignore_index`; a compiled graph cannot raise on a value fed after it was built, so that sample's loss is NaN (policy B) and nothing outside the class axis is read.

members.extended:
`MpsBuilder` is the OOP shape behind the 5 `compile_*` free
functions above.  Each free function above is now a thin
forwarder that constructs a transient `MpsBuilder` and
dispatches to the matching method.  The free-function signatures
are preserved for binding stability — Python (and the cache) still
import them by name.

**Lifetime.** One `MpsBuilder` per compile call.  The class
owns:
  * Reference to the `TraceGraph` and `external_feeds` map.
  * The in-progress `MPSGraph*` (held as `void*` in this pure-C++
    header; the `.mm` re-casts via `__bridge`).
  * The `BuilderContext` that emitters write into.
  * A scratch `std::string* error_msg` pointer for failure
    reporting; populated on failure return.

**Construction.** The constructor takes the same three arguments
shared by every public method: `graph`, `external_feeds`, and
the optional `error_msg`.  It does *not* do any MPSGraph work —
the MPSGraph is created lazily inside each `compile_<mode>`
method.  This keeps construction lightweight (the free-function
forwarders create an instance even when validation rejects the
call) and avoids leaking an MPSGraph allocation on early-exit
paths.

**Why a class rather than 5 free functions.**  The 5 functions
shared ~60% scaffolding expressed as copy-paste (device check,
emitter precheck, placeholder creation, emit loop, target
construction, MPSGraph compile).  Grouping them as methods on a
shared class lets future shared-scaffolding refactors land in one
place rather than in 5 lock-stepped diffs.  The 5 methods
intentionally remain as distinct entry points rather than virtual
dispatch — the divergence between forward-only / forward-bwd /
fused-step / generic-fused-step / variables is finite-state, not
hierarchical.

methods.summary: Op name handled by this emitter — matched against `OpNode::name`.

members.summary: Abstract emitter — one per op family.
members.extended:
Concrete subclasses live in this directory (`Linear.mm`,
`Conv.mm`, …).  Each subclass registers itself at process startup
via `register_emitter`.

Emitter contract
----------------
`OpEmitter::emit` returns `bool` and is responsible for binding
each of its outputs explicitly via `BuilderContext::bind`.
Single-output ops bind `node.outputs[0].id`; multi-output ops
(`split`, `topk`, `lstm`, ...) bind every consumed slot
`node.outputs[k].id`.  The builder does **not** auto-bind —
emitters own their output namespace.  `true` signals success;
`false` signals "unsupported under this configuration" and the
builder aborts the compile, marking the trace signature eager-only.

This symmetric design matches `VjpEmitter::emit` (which
writes input gradients via `BackwardContext::accumulate_grad`
and also returns `bool`).  A single mental model for both emitter
families: *resolve inputs from context, build subgraph, bind
outputs into context, return success*.

members.name: OpNode
members.summary: One recorded op in the trace.
notes:
Aggregate — no methods, no invariants enforced at construction.
The Tracer is responsible for maintaining well-formedness (no
dangling input ids, output ids in monotone increasing order).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Op name as passed to `OpScopeFull` (e.g. `"conv2d"`, `"layer_norm"`).  Matches the schema name in `OpRegistry`.

attributes.name: inputs
attributes.description: Ids of input tensors, in op-defined order.  Phase 1.1 records these by appending to the vector after the backend dispatch returns (the Tracer hook in `OpScopeFull` runs at op entry; input wiring happens later in `wire_autograd`). An `OpNode` with a pending input slot indicates an op that did not go through `wire_autograd` — the builder treats that as an eager-only signature.

attributes.name: outputs
attributes.description: Per-output metadata snapshots.  Phase 1.1 has at most one output per node; the vector is generic so multi-output ops (e.g. `topk`, `lstm`) can be added without IR changes.

attributes.name: attrs
attributes.description: Optional payload keyed by attribute name.  Populated by op forwards via `OpScopeFull::set_attr` when the emitter needs context that can't be recovered from input + output shapes alone (permutation, axes, stride, padding, eps, …).

members.name: OptimizerSpec
members.summary: Optimizer spec passed to `compile_fused_training_step`.
members.extended:
The C++ side directly emits MPSGraph ops for the update rule, using
the auto-derived gradient tensors + a small set of state buffer
feeds (m / v for Adam-family, momentum for SGD).  Per-step scalars
(bias-correction factors for Adam) are passed as additional external
feeds at run time so that one cached executable covers the whole
training loop without recompiles.

members.name: RngRecipe
members.summary: How a traced draw was made.  `a` / `b` are low / high (uniform), mean / std (normal), p (bernoulli) or keep probability / scale (a dropout mask, drawn as dropout draws it and scaled by 1/keep); `lo` / `hi` bound randint.

members.name: TensorMeta
members.summary: Metadata snapshot of a tensor at the moment it appears in the trace.
notes:
Aggregate — copyable, comparable by member-wise equality.  No
inheritance and no virtual members so the value can be stored in a
`std::vector` with no indirection.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: Stable id assigned by the Tracer.  Used by `OpNode` to reference inputs and outputs without owning the underlying `TensorImpl`.

attributes.name: shape
attributes.description: Output shape at trace time.  Phase 1.2 emits MPSGraph placeholders with this shape; Phase 1.6 substitutes batch dim with `-1` for `dynamic=True`.

attributes.name: dtype
attributes.description: Element dtype.  Drives F16 vs F32 placeholder choice when the builder consults `current_amp_policy`.

attributes.name: device
attributes.description: Device of the original tensor.  The builder rejects traces containing mixed-device ops; a single `TraceGraph` runs on one device.

members.name: TraceGraph
members.summary: Ordered list of `OpNode` records produced by one trace.
notes:
Aggregate.  Phase 1.2 attaches an `MpsBuilder` cache entry
keyed by `hash(ops)` rather than mutating this struct.

attributes.name: ops
attributes.description: Nodes appended in dispatch order.  The list defines a DAG via tensor ids — node `j` depends on node `i` iff one of `ops[j].inputs` equals one of the ids in `ops[i].outputs`.

attributes.name: next_id
attributes.description: Monotonic counter the Tracer uses to mint fresh ids when wiring outputs.  Owned by `TraceGraph` so concurrent traces on different threads have independent id spaces.

members.name: TraceId

methods.name: TraceId
methods.signature: void TraceId()

members.summary: Stable named-int identifier minted by `Tracer` for each distinct `TensorImpl` observed during a trace.  Unique within one `TraceGraph` only — never reused, never persisted.
members.extended:
**Design.**  `TraceId` is a named `std::int64_t` rather than a
raw alias so that:

* The trace-id namespace is greppable as a type (e.g. find every
    function that takes a `TraceId` parameter).
  * Hash specialization is bound to this type (no accidental
    overload conflicts with other 64-bit identifiers).
  * Future strict-typing upgrades (e.g. removing implicit
    conversion to `int64_t` to prevent passing a raw int where
    a TraceId is expected) only require flipping the `operator
    std::int64_t()` conversion.  All call sites are already
    compile-time-verified to use the named type.

**Implicit conversion.**  We deliberately preserve implicit
conversion to/from `std::int64_t` for the first pass — there are
~400 call sites across the compile path that mix raw ints (Python
bindings, monotonic counter arithmetic, sentinel `-1` checks)
with TraceId.  Switching to `explicit` would force a parallel
migration we can do in a follow-up.  The named type still moves
the codebase forward and unblocks the audit-flagged improvement.

**Sentinel.**  `TraceId::external_feed()` (== -1) signals "not
produced by any traced op" — i.e. an external feed (model
parameter or user input).  Use `id == TraceId::external_feed()`
in new code; `id.v < 0` still works for backwards compat.

members.name: TraceIdMap
members.summary: Bidirectional mapping between a trace's raw `TensorId` values and the canonical first-appearance numbering minted by `make_cache_key`.
members.extended:
The session `ExecutableCache` stores each cached executable with
its `input_ids` and `output_ids` translated into canonical indices
`0 .. to_raw.size() - 1` via `canonicalize_executable`, and each
caller of `compile_or_cached` receives a copy relabelled into that
caller's own raw `TensorId` space via `localize_executable`.
Without this translation, a session-cache hit returned an executable
whose `input_ids` / `output_ids` carried the *first* trace's raw ids
— which either failed feed lookup in the second trace (silently dropping
the second callable to eager) or bound feeds in the wrong order when an
earlier RNG draw or folded constant shifted raw ids (LCD-454).

methods.signature: void on_op_enter(int name, Device device, Dtype dtype, int shape)
methods.summary: Records the entry of a new op into the active scope.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Op name as passed to `OpScopeFull`.  Copied into the resulting `OpNode::name`.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Device on which the op is dispatching.  Stored in the single `TensorMeta` appended to `outputs`.

parameters.description: Output element dtype at op entry.

notes:
Phase 1.1 appends one `OpNode` per call with an empty
`inputs` vector and a single-element `outputs` vector.
Phase 1.2 backfills `inputs` from the autograd wiring site
and may append additional outputs for multi-output ops.

methods.name: on_op_io
methods.signature: void on_op_io(const int & inputs, const int & output)
methods.summary: Wires the input/output TensorImpl identities of the most recently recorded `OpNode` into the trace IR.

parameters.name: inputs
parameters.description: Owning shared pointers to the input tensors in op-defined order.  `nullptr` slots (e.g. an optional bias) are passed through as `-1` in the resulting `OpNode::inputs``. The Tracer retains a strong reference to every external feed (input not produced by an earlier traced op) so the `MpsBuilder` can read its shape/dtype + the run path can bind its data buffer.

parameters.name: output
parameters.description: Output tensor.  The id minted earlier by `on_op_enter` (stored in `node.outputs[0].id`) is associated with this pointer in the internal map so subsequent ops that consume this tensor can resolve it back to the same id.  Only the raw pointer is kept (no strong ref) — the output's lifetime is the caller's responsibility.

notes:
Phase 1.1 wires only kernel families that go through
`kernel::NaryKernel` or `kernel::VariadicKernel`'s
`wire_autograd` boundary (Conv / Linear / BatchNorm / Norm /
Loss / …).  Ops dispatched through `UnaryKernel` or
`BinaryKernel`'s in-line `forward()` reach
`on_op_enter` but skip this step — their `inputs` slot
stays empty, marking the node "pending" for the Phase 1.2
builder, which then routes that signature to the eager path.

Calling this with an empty `TraceGraph` (no preceding
`on_op_enter`) is a no-op — defensive against ordering
mistakes at hook sites.

methods.signature: int buffer_value(const int & buffer)

methods.signature: void on_op_attr(int key, int value)
methods.summary: Attach a single attribute to the most recently recorded `OpNode`.  Used by op forwards via `OpScopeFull::set_attr` to thread payloads (permutation, axis, stride, padding, …) that the emitter would otherwise be unable to recover from inputs + output shapes alone.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Attribute name; chosen by the op forward and read by the matching emitter.  Convention: snake_case, matches the reference-framework keyword argument when one exists (`"permutation"`, `"stride"`, `"padding"`, `"axis"`, `"keepdim"`, `"eps"`, …).

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The payload, moved into the attribute map.

notes:
Calling this with an empty `TraceGraph` (no preceding
`on_op_enter`) is a no-op — defensive against ordering
mistakes at hook sites.  Overwrites any prior value under
`key` on the same node, so duplicate calls report the last
value (matches `unordered_map` semantics).

methods.name: on_rng_feed
methods.signature: void on_rng_feed(int name, const int & output)
methods.summary: Records `output` — just drawn by the RNG op `name` — as an external feed instead of as that op's output, and drops the op's node: the executable takes the draw as an input, and `redraw_rng_feeds` draws it again on every run.  See `RngFeeds.h`.

methods.name: mark_unsupported
methods.signature: void mark_unsupported(int why)
methods.summary: Marks the recording as one no executable can stand for (see `TraceGraph::unsupported`).  The first reason given is kept.

methods.name: redraw_rng
methods.signature: bool redraw_rng()
methods.summary: Whether a draw from the default generator becomes a feed drawn again on every run (the compile path, `RngFeeds.h`) — on by default — or stays an op in the recording.  Core ML export turns it off: it lifts each recorded draw into a model input, which needs the op.

methods.name: set_redraw_rng
methods.signature: void set_redraw_rng(bool on)

methods.name: fold_constants
methods.signature: bool fold_constants()
methods.summary: Whether an op that reads nothing the trace sees is left out of the recording: its output stays unseen, and an op that the trace does record reads it as one constant feed, already on that op's device. `lucid.tensor([...]).to(x.device)` then costs a feed, not a CPU op in a Metal trace (which ran the whole call eagerly).  Off by default, because "unseen" means "constant" only to a consumer that watches every live tensor the call reads — its arguments and its model's state.  The optimizer, decode and segmented tracers do not, and an op on their state would be frozen at its trace-time value; Core ML export folds on its own, knowing which shapes follow a flexible input.  `lucid.compile.compile` turns it on.

methods.name: set_fold_constants
methods.signature: void set_fold_constants(bool on)

methods.name: on_factory
methods.signature: void on_factory(const int & out)
methods.summary: `out` was made from nothing by the op now recording — a factory (`zeros` / `arange` / `eye` …), never a random draw.  With folding on and `out` off Metal, the op is left out and `out` is a constant; on Metal the compiled graph makes it itself, and otherwise nothing changes.

methods.name: made_here
methods.signature: bool made_here(const TensorImpl * impl)
methods.summary: Whether `impl` is a constant the trace made itself — a factory's output, or a left-out op's — which no tensor outside the trace shares.

methods.name: on_host_read
methods.signature: void on_host_read(const TensorImpl * impl)
methods.summary: A value the trace knows — an op's output, an input, a parameter or a random draw — read on the host (`item` / `tolist` / `numpy`, and so `float(t)` or `if t > 0`).  What the host does with it is invisible to the recording, which would bake this call's value into every later one: the trace is marked unsupported.  A tensor the trace has not seen — a constant made on the spot — is left alone.

methods.name: watch
methods.signature: void watch(const int & impl)
methods.summary: `impl` is an argument of the traced call.  Its values are the call's data before any op has consumed it, so `on_host_read` treats a read of it as a read of a traced value from the start of the trace.

methods.name: on_derived
methods.signature: void on_derived(int name, const int & srcs, const int & out)
methods.summary: `out` was made from `src` outside the op dispatcher — a device transfer, an alias with other autograd flags, a shared-buffer relabel (the TensorImpl bindings, `bind_tensor.cpp`).  When the trace knows `src`, `out` is recorded as op `name` reading it, so a later op or host read of `out` reaches the traced value.  Unrecorded, `out` was a tensor the trace had never seen: a host read of it went unnoticed, and an op reading it took it as a feed pinned at its trace-time value — every compiled call answered with the first call's data.  `name` is an emitter's when `out` holds `src`'s values on `src`'s device (`"detach"`); any other name has no emitter and sends the call to eager.  A `src` the trace has not seen is a constant to it, and so is `out`: nothing is recorded.  With several sources (a fused kernel, a custom Metal kernel) the op reads all of them, and is recorded when the trace sees any one.

methods.name: on_inplace_write
methods.signature: void on_inplace_write(const int & target, const int & value)
methods.summary: `target` now holds what `value` holds: an in-place op computed `value` out of place and spliced it into `target` (`TensorImpl::take_storage_from` / `write_through`).  Later reads of `target` resolve to `value`'s id — without this, `a.mul_(b) .add_(c)` recorded the add reading `a` from before the mul.  A target from outside the trace keeps its feed id in `external_feeds` while its current id moves, which is how a write to a buffer is found (`lucid/compile/_core/buffer_writes.py`); one the trace has not read yet becomes a feed first.  A value the trace has not seen becomes a feed of its own.

methods.name: restore_outside_writes
methods.signature: void restore_outside_writes()
methods.summary: Puts every tensor from outside the trace that the trace wrote in place back to its value from before the trace, from the copy `on_inplace_write` kept at the first write.  The trace-time call ran those writes eagerly; whatever runs next — an executable or an eager fallback — applies them itself, and would otherwise apply them twice.  Call once the trace has finished.

The Tracer holds an owning `TensorImplPtr` for every
external feed so the underlying buffers cannot be released

`live_refs_` already owns each `TensorImpl` observed

A buffer written in place carries the id it had when the mapping

methods.name: ~VjpEmitter
methods.signature: void ~VjpEmitter()

methods.name: op_name
methods.signature: int op_name()
methods.summary: Op name this VJP handles — matched against `OpNode::name`.

methods.name: emit
methods.signature: bool emit(BackwardContext & bctx, const OpNode & fwd_node, const int & grad_outs)
methods.summary: Emit the backward MPSGraph subgraph for `fwd_node`.

parameters.name: bctx
parameters.description: Carries the in-progress graph + grad id map + fwd lookups.

parameters.name: fwd_node
parameters.description: The forward node being differentiated.  Read inputs / outputs / attrs the same way the forward emitter did.

parameters.name: grad_outs
parameters.description: One incoming gradient per forward output slot, in `fwd_node.outputs` order.  `nullptr` entries indicate dead output slots — the VJP must not produce contributions that depend on a dead-slot grad (most ops just check `grad_outs[0] != nullptr` and bail otherwise).

returns.description: `true` on success.  `false` signals a per-call coverage gap (rare — typically the VJP doesn't support some attr combination); the walker aborts and the caller falls through to MPSGraph autograd (or hard-fails under `LUCID_MANUAL_VJP_REQUIRE`).

members.summary: Abstract VJP emitter — one per op family.
members.extended:
Concrete subclasses live under `VjpEmitters/<bucket>/` and
register themselves at process startup.  The trace-IR conventions
mirror `OpEmitter` 1:1 (input slots from
`fwd_node.inputs`, output slots from `fwd_node.outputs`, attrs
from `fwd_node.attrs`).

Forward vs backward signature
-----------------------------
`OpEmitter::emit` returns `void*` (the single primary
output tensor; auto-bound by the builder).  This emitter returns
`bool` because backward emission is fundamentally many-output:
a binary op's VJP writes grads for two inputs, a 3-input
`linear`'s VJP writes three.  Rather than picking a "primary"
grad to return, every VJP writes its outputs via
`BackwardContext::accumulate_grad` and returns `true` on
success.  Returning `false` signals a per-call coverage gap —
rare, e.g. an attr combination the VJP doesn't support — which
the walker propagates back to the integration site for
fall-through to `gradientForPrimaryTensor:` (or hard-fail under
`LUCID_MANUAL_VJP_REQUIRE=1`).

members.name: VjpRegion
members.summary: Custom backward subgraph captured for a `lucid.autograd.Function` with `_traced_backward = True`.
members.extended:
Forward ops in `[fwd_begin, fwd_end)` compute the forward outputs
`output_metas` from `input_ids`.  During backward emission,
`BackwardWalker` skips per-op VJP emission for
`ops[fwd_begin .. fwd_end)` and instead binds each output's resolved
upstream cotangent (or a zero tensor when unused) to `cotangent_ids[j]`,
emits `bwd_ops` through the forward op emitters, and accumulates each
non-negative `input_grad_ids[k]` onto `input_ids[k]`.

methods.name: add_grouped_lut_const
methods.signature: void add_grouped_lut_const(const int & name, const MilTensorType & output_type, int indices_offset, MilDataType indices_dtype, int lut_offset, MilDataType lut_dtype, const int & lut_shape)
methods.summary: A weight stored as int8 codes plus a per-channel scale, dequantized on the way into whatever consumes it.
methods.extended:
Core ML spells this `constexpr_affine_dequantize`, and it is not
shaped like other operations: the codes, the scale, the zero point
and the axis are *attributes*, not operands, so it cannot go through
`add_op`.  `scale_bytes` and `zero_point_bytes` are the raw
little-endian payloads — the schema carries both as `bytes`, which
is how a float16 scale and an int8 zero point fit the same field.
A weight stored as indices into one or more palettes
(`constexpr_lut_to_dense`).  Both payloads live in the blob and
are named by inline arguments rather than by attributes, which is
what separates this from the iOS16 spelling of the same operation.

`indices_dtype` is a sub-byte key type and carries the weight's
own shape.  `lut_shape` is `[groups..., 1 << n_bits, 1]`: one
table per group of output channels, so a convolution whose
channels differ in magnitude by orders of magnitude does not have
to spend a single table on all of them.  A single group is the
per-tensor case.

Using this raises the model's opset, and so its deployment floor,
the same way carrying state does.

methods.summary: A weight stored as its non-zero values plus a bit mask (`constexpr_sparse_to_dense`).  Both ride in the blob: the mask is one bit per element, which is small but not small enough to want inline.

methods.name: add_sparse_const_extended
methods.signature: void add_sparse_const_extended(const int & name, const MilTensorType & output_type, int nonzero_offset, int nonzero_count, MilDataType nonzero_dtype, int mask_offset)
methods.summary: The same operation in its iOS18 spelling: payloads named by inline arguments rather than attributes, and the mask typed `UINT1` carrying the weight's own shape instead of a byte count.
methods.extended:
Both forms exist because both are needed. A program that declares
`CoreML7` must use the older one, and a program that has been
raised to `CoreML8` by some other feature — carrying state, say
— must use this one: Core ML's loader does not reject the older
spelling there, it crashes on it.

members.summary: Threadgroup geometry for `run_metal_kernel`.
members.extended:
Mirrors the two `MTLSize` arguments passed to
`dispatchThreadgroups:threadsPerThreadgroup:` — the outer grid
of threadgroups and the per-threadgroup thread count, both in 3-D.
notes:
Total threads launched = product(grid) * product(threads).  Callers
are responsible for sizing this to cover `output_shape`.

attributes.name: grid
attributes.description: Threadgroup grid extent (x, y, z).  Defaults to `{1, 1, 1}`.

members.name: MetalBuffer
members.summary: Plain descriptor for a Metal buffer that backs Lucid's `SharedStorage`.
members.extended:
Holds the raw CPU pointer + opaque MTL handle + size for a Metal
shared-memory buffer.  This struct does not own anything — lifetime is
managed externally (see `OwnedMetalBuffer` for the RAII form).
On Apple Silicon, `cpu_ptr` and `mtl_handle` reference the **same
physical pages**, so CPU writes are immediately visible to GPU kernels
(and vice versa) without an explicit transfer.

**See Also**

`OwnedMetalBuffer` — RAII wrapper around this descriptor.
notes:
Use `make_metal_shared` for everyday allocation — manual
pairing of `allocate_shared` and `deallocate_shared` is
only needed for low-level pool code.

attributes.description: CPU-accessible virtual address of the buffer.  `nullptr` if the buffer is uninitialised or has been deallocated.

attributes.name: mtl_handle
attributes.description: Opaque `CFRetain`'d `id<MTLBuffer>` cast to `void*` to keep this header free of Objective-C types.  `nullptr` when invalid.

attributes.name: nbytes
attributes.description: Allocation size in bytes.  Always `0` on an uninitialised value.

members.summary: RAII handle for a compiled Metal compute pipeline.
members.extended:
Wraps a `MTLComputePipelineState` plus its dedicated
`MTLCommandQueue` (both `CFRetain`-ed) so that one pipeline can
be invoked many times without re-compiling MSL source.  The Obj-C
types are erased to `void*` here to keep this header includable
from plain C++.  Non-copyable, move-only.

**See Also**

`compile_metal_kernel` — factory that produces these.
`run_metal_kernel` — invokes the compiled pipeline.

Released in `release_`.  Move constructors null out the
source so the destructor only releases once.

`std::shared_ptr` whose custom deleter calls
`deallocate_shared` when the last reference drops.  Used by
`SharedStorage` to express ref-counted shared GPU/CPU memory.

**See Also**

`make_metal_shared` — the factory that produces these.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.description: Ref-counted owner that releases `buf` on last drop.  Type- erased to `void` because the deleter, not the type, carries the cleanup logic.

members.name: SlicePlan
members.summary: The member as a strided slice of the root reshaped to `dims`: the plan slice_update needs, or false when the geometry is not one.
members.extended:
The member's axes longer than one, ordered by stride, outermost first,
become the slice's axes.  Every axis but the innermost steps by one over
a root axis as long as the next axis's stride; the innermost steps by its
own stride over a root axis of unit stride.  That works when each stride
divides the one before it, the root's size divides by the outermost, and
every axis's run stays inside its root axis.

members.summary: Abstract base interface every Lucid op kernel implements.
members.extended:
`IKernel` exposes a minimal polymorphic surface so the
autograd engine, profiler, and testing harnesses can manipulate
kernels without knowing the concrete CRTP type.  Concrete kernels
inherit `IKernel` indirectly via one of the CRTP helpers
(`UnaryKernel`, `BinaryKernel`, `NaryKernel`,
`VariadicKernel`); the CRTP layer supplies correct overrides
of every virtual below.

**See Also**

`UnaryKernel`, `BinaryKernel`, `NaryKernel`,
`VariadicKernel` — CRTP helpers that provide the typed
implementations of `apply` and (when applicable) `compute`.
`KernelPolicy` — documentation of the compile-time flags
concrete kernels expose to the CRTP layer.
notes:
The interface is intentionally split: `compute` is the generic
polymorphic forward entry point, while `apply` is the backward
entry point called by the autograd engine during reverse-mode
differentiation.  In practice nearly every op routes its forward
through its CRTP base's typed static `forward()` (which handles
dtype promotion, contiguity, dispatch and graph wiring) and uses
`compute` only when invoked through a fully generic harness.

Thread safety: instances are **not** thread-safe.  The framework
constructs a fresh kernel per forward invocation and never shares
it across threads.

members.name: KernelPolicy
members.summary: Documentation-only enumeration of the compile-time policy flags a concrete kernel may override on its CRTP base.
members.extended:
Derived kernels do not instantiate this struct — they override the
equivalent `static constexpr bool kSavesInput` / `kSavesOutput` /
`kHasGradient` members on `UnaryKernel` (or sibling bases).
`KernelPolicy` exists purely so the flag set is documented
in one place and discoverable via codegen tools.

**See Also**

`IKernel` — the abstract base these flags refine.
`UnaryKernel`, `BinaryKernel` — CRTP bases that read
these flags via `Derived::kSavesInput` etc.

attributes.name: saves_inputs
attributes.description: Whether `forward()` snapshots the input storages into `saved_inputs_` for later use in `apply()` / `grad_formula`. Set `false` for ops whose backward formula does not need the forward inputs (e.g. `Add` whose backward is the identity).

attributes.name: saves_output
attributes.description: Whether `forward()` additionally snapshots the output storage into `saved_output_`.  Useful for ops whose backward is expressed more cheaply in terms of the output (e.g. `ReLU`, `Softmax`, `Pow`).

attributes.name: has_gradient
attributes.description: Whether the op participates in autograd at all.  Setting `false` skips graph wiring entirely — used by in-place / non-differentiable ops such as integer cast or copy.

attributes.name: deterministic
attributes.description: Whether the op produces bit-identical outputs for bit-identical inputs.  Currently informational only; consumed by future determinism-mode validators.

methods.name: wire_autograd
methods.signature: bool wire_autograd(int bwd, const int & inputs, const int & out, const int & saves)
methods.summary: Attach an existing backward node to the autograd graph.

parameters.name: bwd
parameters.description: The backward node instance to install on `out`.

parameters.name: inputs
parameters.description: The forward inputs in canonical order.  Slots may be `nullptr` (e.g. an optional bias).

parameters.name: saves
parameters.description: Which inputs the backward reads the values of: input `i`'s storage is snapshotted into `saved_inputs_[i]` when `saves[i]` and the input is non-null.  Those are the inputs `AutogradNode::validate_versions` guards, so an input read by shape alone — a bias, a `beta` — is left out, and a write into it after forward is not refused.

returns.description: `true` when the autograd graph was wired and `out` had its `grad_fn` installed; `false` when grad mode is off or no input requires a gradient (no-op).

notes:
Side effects on success: populates `bwd`'s dtype/device/output
shape from the first non-null input, fills `input_shapes_`,
`input_tensors_`, `saved_inputs_`, `saved_impl_inputs_`,
records one `Edge` per input via `detail::ensure_grad_fn`,
captures per-input versions for in-place mutation detection, and
marks `out` as a non-leaf, requires_grad tensor.

methods.name: capture_inputs
methods.signature: void capture_inputs(Derived & bwd, const int & inputs, const int & saves)

members.summary: CRTP base for fixed-arity `N`-input op kernels.
members.extended:
Inherits `AutogradNode\<Derived, N\>` so input metadata
(`input_shapes_`, `saved_inputs_`, `input_tensors_`,
`saved_impl_inputs_`) is stored in compile-time-sized
`std::array` containers.  Also inherits `IKernel` for
polymorphic invocation.

Unlike `UnaryKernel` and `BinaryKernel`, this base does
**not** provide a `forward()` trampoline — N-ary ops have too much
op-specific validation to share a single template.  Instead, derived
ops own their `forward()` and call `wire_autograd` once the
output tensor exists to attach the backward node.

Template Parameters
-------------------
Derived : class
    The concrete CRTP self-type.
N : std::size_t
    The fixed input arity.  Typically 3 or more (use
    `BinaryKernel` for `N == 2`).

**See Also**

`UnaryKernel`, `BinaryKernel`, `VariadicKernel`.

so the saved-input and edge containers can grow at runtime, and

members.name: allocate_aligned_bytes
members.summary: Allocates an aligned, optionally-pooled byte buffer of `nbytes`.
members.extended:
The returned `shared_ptr<std::byte[]>` owns the block via a custom
deleter that either (a) returns the block to the thread-local pool —
for CPU allocations up to 4 MB whose class still has free slots — or
(b) calls `std::free` directly, for large allocations, full pool
slots, and non-CPU devices.  In both paths the deleter also fires the
matching `MemoryTracker::track_free` hook.

On every successful allocation the matching
`MemoryTracker::track_alloc` hook is fired, so per-device
counters stay in sync with the live byte total.

parameters.name: nbytes
parameters.description: Number of bytes to allocate.  A value of `0` returns an empty `shared_ptr` (no allocation, no tracker update).

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Device tag controlling (a) which `MemoryTracker` counter bank is updated and (b) whether the pool path is taken — only `Device::CPU` is poolable.  Defaults to `Device::CPU`.

returns.description: Owning handle to a `kCpuAlignment`-aligned byte buffer at least `nbytes` long.  Empty when `nbytes == 0`.  The capacity may exceed `nbytes` for pooled allocations (rounded up to the next power of two ≥ `kCpuAlignment`).

raises.description: `posix_memalign` failed.  The exception carries the requested size, the current live bytes, and the historical peak for the target device so the caller can format an informative message.

examples:
auto block = allocate_aligned_bytes(1024);                // CPU, pooled
    auto huge  = allocate_aligned_bytes(64 << 20);            // CPU, bypass pool
    auto gpu   = allocate_aligned_bytes(N, Device::GPU);      // GPU, tracker only
notes:
The pool is **thread-local**, so allocation and deallocation are
lock-free on the fast path.  Cached blocks are released when the
owning thread exits.  Blocks freed on a different thread than the
one that allocated them still work correctly, but they will be
returned to the freeing thread's pool — long-running thread-pool
workloads with cross-thread tensor ownership may therefore observe
slight imbalance in retained free-list size.

members.name: atan2_op
members.signature: int atan2_op(const int & y, const int & x)
members.summary: Quadrant-aware arctangent: $y = \mathrm{atan2}(y_\text{in}, x_\text{in})$.
members.extended:
Composite over `arctan_op` plus `where_op` branches that
patch the result with $\pm \pi$ / $\pm \pi/2$ / $0$ corrections based on
the signs of the operands.  The divide $y / x$ is guarded by
substituting $1$ for $x = 0$ so the safe branch is always defined.
Gradient flows through the underlying primitives.

**Math**

$$
  \mathrm{atan2}(y, x) =
  \begin{cases}
    \arctan(y/x) & x > 0 \\
    \arctan(y/x) + \pi & x < 0,\ y \ge 0 \\
    \arctan(y/x) - \pi & x < 0,\ y < 0 \\
    +\pi/2 & x = 0,\ y > 0 \\
    -\pi/2 & x = 0,\ y < 0 \\
    0 & x = 0,\ y = 0
  \end{cases}
$$

**See Also**

`arctan_op`.

returns.description: Angles in $[-\pi, \pi]$ on the broadcast shape of `y` and `x`.

fixed at `KL` regardless of how many positions fall on padding (pad
values contribute `0` to the sum but still count toward the divisor).
This matches the count-include-pad convention used by the reference
framework's default `AvgPool1d`.

**Math**

$$y_{b,c,o} = \frac{1}{\text{KL}} \sum_{k=0}^{\text{KL}-1}
  x_{b,c,\,o\cdot \text{stride\_l} + k - \text{pad\_l}}.$$

members.extended:
Inverse of `im2col_1d_f32`: scatter-adds each column of `cols` back

members.signature: void im2col_1d_f32(const float * x, float * cols, int C, int L, int KL, int OL, int stride_l, int pad_l, int dilation_l)
members.summary: Single-precision 1-D im2col unfold.
members.extended:
Unfolds each length-$KL$ receptive field of a 1-D feature map into a
column of a 2-D matrix so that conv1d can be expressed as a single GEMM.
Out-of-bounds positions (from padding or dilation) are written as zero.

**Math**

For each output index $o \in [0, OL)$, channel $c$ and kernel offset $k$:
$$ \text{cols}[c \cdot KL + k, o] = x[c, o \cdot \text{stride} + k \cdot \text{dilation} - \text{pad}] $$
with zero for out-of-bounds positions.

parameters.description: Convolution stride / zero-padding / dilation along the spatial axis.

notes:
Memory layout assumes the standard NCHW-style channel-first convention,
with the batch dimension handled at the caller (loop over $N$).

members.name: im2col_f32
members.signature: void im2col_f32(const float * x, float * cols, int C, int H, int W, int KH, int KW, int OH, int OW, int stride_h, int stride_w, int pad_h, int pad_w, int dilation_h, int dilation_w)
members.summary: Single-precision 2-D im2col unfold.
members.extended:
Unfolds the 2-D feature map $x$ of shape $(C, H, W)$ into a matrix where
each column is a $K_H \times K_W$ receptive-field patch flattened across
channels.  The output column matrix has shape $(C \cdot K_H \cdot K_W,
O_H \cdot O_W)$ so that conv2d = `sgemm(W_reshape, cols)`.

Out-of-bounds positions (those reaching outside the input due to padding,
stride, or dilation) are written as zero.

**Math**

For each output position $(o_h, o_w)$, kernel offset $(k_h, k_w)$ and
channel $c$, the corresponding input position is
$$ i_h = o_h \cdot s_h + k_h \cdot d_h - p_h, \quad i_w = o_w \cdot s_w + k_w \cdot d_w - p_w $$
and `cols[c \cdot K_H K_W + k_h K_W + k_w, o_h \cdot O_W + o_w] = x[c, i_h, i_w]` (zero if OOB).

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Input tensor, shape $(C, H, W)$ row-major.

parameters.name: cols
parameters.description: Output column matrix, shape $(C \cdot K_H \cdot K_W, O_H \cdot O_W)$.

notes:
Memory layout is NCHW (channel-first) — the batch dimension is iterated
at the caller, with one im2col per batch element.

members.name: lapack_cholesky_f32
members.signature: void lapack_cholesky_f32(float * A, int n, bool lower, int * info)
members.summary: Single-precision Cholesky decomposition (in place).
members.extended:
Factors a symmetric positive-definite matrix into either $A = L L^T$
(`lower=true`) or $A = U^T U$ (`lower=false`).  After the LAPACK call
the off-triangle entries are zeroed so the result is a clean lower / upper
matrix.

**Math**

$$ A = L L^T \quad\text{or}\quad A = U^T U $$

**References**

LAPACK `spotrf_`.

parameters.description: Row-major $n \times n$ symmetric positive-definite matrix; overwritten by the requested triangular factor.

parameters.name: lower
parameters.description: `true` for lower triangular $L$, `false` for upper triangular $U$.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: LAPACK status (`> 0` means $A$ is not positive definite at column `info`).

members.name: lapack_eig_f32
members.signature: void lapack_eig_f32(const float * A, int n, float * wr, float * wi, float * VR, int * info)
members.summary: General (non-symmetric) eigendecomposition (float32).
members.extended:
Computes eigenvalues of a general real matrix; complex eigenvalues are
returned as separate real (`wr`) and imaginary (`wi`) parts.  Right
eigenvectors (columns of $V$) are written to `VR` if non-null.

**Math**

$$ A v_j = \lambda_j v_j, \quad \lambda_j = \mathrm{wr}_j + i \, \mathrm{wi}_j $$

**References**

LAPACK `sgeev_`.

parameters.name: wr, wi
parameters.description: Real / imaginary parts of the eigenvalues, length $n$.

parameters.name: VR
parameters.description: Right-eigenvector matrix (row-major) or `nullptr` to skip vectors.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: LAPACK status (`> 0` = QR iteration failed to converge).

members.summary: Symmetric eigendecomposition (float32) via divide-and-conquer.
members.extended:
For a real symmetric input $A = A^T$, computes the spectral decomposition
$A = V \, \mathrm{diag}(w) \, V^T$.  Eigenvalues are produced in ascending
order and eigenvectors are the columns of $V$ (returned row-major after
transposition).

$$ A V = V \, \mathrm{diag}(w) $$

members.signature: void lapack_lstsq_f32(const float * A, float * B, int m, int n, int nrhs, int * info)
members.summary: Single-precision least-squares solver via QR.
members.extended:
Computes the minimum-2-norm solution of an overdetermined system:
$$ \min_X \|A X - B\|_2 $$

overwritten with $X$ in its leading $n$ rows.

members.name: lapack_svd_f32
members.signature: void lapack_svd_f32(const float * A, int m, int n, bool full_matrices, float * U, float * S, float * Vt, int * info)
members.summary: Single-precision singular value decomposition via divide-and-conquer.
members.extended:
Computes $A = U \, \mathrm{diag}(S) \, V^T$.  When `full_matrices` is
false the thin SVD is returned: $U \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times k}$,
$V^T \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$, $k = \min(m, n)$.  When true the full
matrices ($U \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times m}$, $V^T \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$)
are returned.

**Math**

$$ A = U \, \Sigma \, V^T, \quad \Sigma = \mathrm{diag}(S) $$

**References**

LAPACK `sgesdd_` (divide-and-conquer driver).

parameters.name: full_matrices
parameters.description: Controls thin vs full SVD as described above.

parameters.name: S
parameters.description: Output singular values in descending order, length $\min(m, n)$.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: LAPACK status (`> 0` = SVD did not converge).

members.name: layer_norm_backward_f32
members.signature: void layer_norm_backward_f32(const float * x, const float * gamma, const float * saved_mean, const float * saved_rstd, const float * g, float * dx, float * dgamma, float * dbeta, int outer, int N)
members.summary: Single-precision LayerNorm backward — produces input, weight, and bias gradients from a saved-tensor forward pass.
members.extended:
Uses the closed-form LayerNorm gradient that avoids recomputing the row
statistics.  `dgamma` and `dbeta` are *accumulated* into the supplied
buffers; callers reducing over multiple sub-batches must zero them once at
the start.  `dx` is written fully (not accumulated).

**Math**

Let $\hat{x}_i = (x_i - \mu)\,\text{rstd}$ and
$\widetilde{g}_i = \gamma_i g_i$.  Then
$$\frac{\partial L}{\partial x_i} =
  \frac{\text{rstd}}{N} \!\left(N \widetilde{g}_i - \sum_j \widetilde{g}_j -
    \hat{x}_i \sum_j \widetilde{g}_j \hat{x}_j\right),$$
$$\frac{\partial L}{\partial \gamma_i} = \sum_{\text{rows}} g_i \hat{x}_i,
  \qquad \frac{\partial L}{\partial \beta_i} = \sum_{\text{rows}} g_i.$$

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Original forward input of shape `(outer, N)`.

parameters.name: g
parameters.description: Upstream gradient $\partial L / \partial y$ of shape `(outer, N)`.

parameters.name: dgamma, dbeta
parameters.description: Output gradients w.r.t. the affine parameters; shape `(N,)`; *accumulated* (caller must zero on first call).

parameters.name: x

parameters.name: saved_mean, saved_rstd

members.name: layer_norm_forward_f32
members.signature: void layer_norm_forward_f32(const float * x, const float * gamma, const float * beta, float * y, float * saved_mean, float * saved_rstd, int outer, int N, double eps)
members.summary: Single-precision LayerNorm forward — normalises every row of length `N` using its empirical mean and variance, then applies a per-feature affine transform $\gamma \hat{x} + \beta$ in the same pass.
members.extended:
The f32 path is a vDSP fast path: it computes the row mean with
`vmean_f32`, centres the row into a scratch buffer with `vsadd_f32`,
derives the variance as a self-dot-product via `vdotpr_f32`, then fuses
the affine into a `vmadd_f32` call so the data is touched twice rather
than three times.  Per-row `mean` and `rstd = 1/sqrt(var + eps)` are
stashed so the backward kernel can skip the recomputation.

**Math**

$$\hat{x}_i = \frac{x_i - \mu}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 + \varepsilon}}, \qquad
  y_i = \gamma_i \hat{x}_i + \beta_i,$$
with $\mu, \sigma^2$ the row mean and variance of `x`.

**References**

[Ba, Kiros & Hinton, "Layer Normalization" ([arXiv:1607.06450](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.06450), 2016)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.06450).

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Input buffer of shape `(outer, N)` in row-major order.

parameters.name: gamma, beta
parameters.description: Per-feature affine parameters of shape `(N,)`.  Both required.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Output buffer of shape `(outer, N)`; written densely.

parameters.name: saved_mean, saved_rstd
parameters.description: Per-row scratch outputs of shape `(outer,)`.  Consumed by `layer_norm_backward_f32`.

parameters.name: outer
parameters.description: Number of independent rows (product of all leading dimensions).

parameters.name: eps
parameters.description: Variance stabiliser; cast to `float` before being added to `var`.

members.name: max_axis_f32
members.signature: void max_axis_f32(const float * in, float * out, int outer, int reduce_dim, int inner)
members.summary: Reduces a single axis by elementwise maximum into a packed `(outer, inner)` output.
members.extended:
The kernel always uses the generic `axis_reduce` template — Accelerate
does not expose a stride-aware vDSP equivalent for `max` with the same
semantics, so vectorisation is left to the compiler.  Initial accumulator
is `-inf` which means an empty reduce dimension yields `-inf` per cell.

**Math**

$$\text{out}[o, i] = \max_{r} \text{in}[o, r, i].$$

parameters.name: in
parameters.description: Source buffer of shape `(outer, reduce_dim, inner)`.

notes:
NaN propagation follows the C++ `a > b` semantics: a NaN on either side
of the comparison loses, so a NaN element will not necessarily survive the
reduction.  Downstream code that requires NaN-poisoning must guard explicitly.

members.name: max_pool1d_forward_f32
members.signature: void max_pool1d_forward_f32(const float * x, float * y, int * argmax, int B, int C, int L, int KL, int OL, int stride_l, int pad_l)
members.summary: Single-precision 1-D max-pool forward over an NCL-laid-out input.
members.extended:
For each output element the kernel scans the corresponding `KL`-wide
window and records both the maximum value into `y` and the *flat*
position within the `L` dimension of the input row into `argmax`.
Out-of-bounds (pad) positions contribute `-inf` and so never win unless
the whole window is padding (in which case the first pad slot wins).

**Shape**

$\text{OL} = \lfloor (L + 2 \cdot \text{pad\_l} - \text{KL}) /
\text{stride\_l}\rfloor + 1$.

**See Also**

max_pool1d_backward_f32 : Reverse pass that consumes `argmax`.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Output tensor of shape `(B, C, OL)`.

parameters.description: Companion buffer of shape `(B, C, OL)` holding the winning `L`-axis index of each output element; consumed by the backward kernel.

parameters.name: B, C, L
parameters.description: Batch, channel, and spatial extents of `x`.

parameters.name: OL
parameters.description: Spatial extent of `y`; caller computes it as `(L + 2*pad_l - KL) / stride_l + 1`.

parameters.description: Window stride and symmetric zero-pad on the `L` axis.
