members.extended:
**Math**

$$a_i \leftarrow a_i^3$$

**See Also**

`cube_op` — out-of-place counterpart.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Tensor to cube in place.  Must be non-null.

returns.description: The same pointer as `a`.

members.name: cube_op
members.summary: Compute $y = x^3$ element-wise.
members.extended:
Allocates a fresh output of the same shape and dtype as `a` and
delegates to `CubeBackward::forward`.

**See Also**

`CubeBackward` — backward node.

returns.description: Output tensor of the same shape and dtype.

members.name: cube_root_op
members.summary: Element-wise cube root — returns $\sqrt[3]{a}$ with a fully wired autograd node.
members.extended:
Defined for all real inputs (positive, zero, and negative); the
negative branch is the real cube root, not the complex principal value.

**Math**

$$y_i = \sqrt[3]{x_i}, \qquad
\frac{\partial y_i}{\partial x_i} = \frac{1}{3 y_i^{2}}$$

**Shape**

Output shape equals input shape (elementwise).

**See Also**

`CubeRootBackward`.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Input tensor (promoted to FP32 by the op schema).

returns.description: Output tensor with the same shape as `a`; gradient is $g / (3 y^{2})$.

examples:
``cube_root_op(-8.0) == -2.0``  (real cube root of a negative number).
``cube_root_op(27.0) == 3.0``.
notes:
CPU implementation uses Accelerate's `vvcbrtf`; GPU uses MLX's
power op with exponent $1/3$.  The gradient is singular at zero —
avoid backpropagating through inputs that touch the origin.

members.name: cummax_op
members.signature: int cummax_op(const int & a, int axis)
members.summary: Inclusive cumulative maximum along a single axis, $y_k = \max_{j \le k} x_j$.
members.extended:
Output is non-decreasing along `axis`.  Backward credits the
upstream gradient $dy_k$ to the position that **first** achieved the
running maximum up to $k$ (i.e. the unique $i \le k$ at which the
running max changed value); positions that merely tie with the
running max receive no gradient.

**Math**

$$
  y_k = \max_{j \le k} x_j, \qquad
  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x_i} =
  \sum_{k \ge i} dy_k \cdot \mathbb{1}[\,i = \arg\max_{j \le k} x_j\,].
$$

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Input tensor of any non-scalar shape; only F32 / F64 are supported by the backward pass.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Axis along which to accumulate (negative wraps).

returns.description: Output tensor of the same shape and dtype as `a`.

notes:
Backward is computed by a right-to-left segmented accumulation on
CPU (or evaluated on CPU after a GPU round-trip).  Saves only the
forward output; the input is not needed.

members.name: cummin_op
members.signature: int cummin_op(const int & a, int axis)
members.summary: Inclusive cumulative minimum along a single axis, $y_k = \min_{j \le k} x_j$.
members.extended:
Symmetric to `cummax_op`: gradient flows only to the position
that first achieved the running minimum at each $k$.

**Math**

$$
  y_k = \min_{j \le k} x_j, \qquad
  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x_i} =
  \sum_{k \ge i} dy_k \cdot \mathbb{1}[\,i = \arg\min_{j \le k} x_j\,].
$$

**See Also**

`cummax_op` — symmetric maximum scan.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Input tensor of any non-scalar shape; backward supports F32 / F64.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Axis along which to accumulate (negative wraps).

returns.description: Output tensor of the same shape and dtype as `a`.

members.name: cumprod_op
members.signature: int cumprod_op(const int & a, int axis)
members.summary: Inclusive cumulative product along a single axis, $y_k = \prod_{j \le k} x_j$.
members.extended:
The output has the same shape and dtype as the input.  Backward
reuses the reverse-cumsum primitive against the saved cumprod
output and divides by the saved input,
$dx = \mathrm{reverse}(\mathrm{cumsum}(\mathrm{reverse}(dy \cdot y)))
/ x$, before the first zero of $x$ along `axis`.

**Math**

$$
  y_k = \prod_{j \le k} x_j, \qquad
  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x_i} =
  \sum_{j \ge i} \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial y_j}
  \cdot \prod_{k \le j,\, k \ne i} x_k.
$$

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Input tensor of any non-scalar shape and real dtype.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Axis along which to accumulate (negative wraps).

returns.description: Output tensor of the same shape and dtype as `a`.

notes:
At the first zero $x_z$ the gradient is
$\prod_{k<z} x_k \sum_{j \ge z} dy_j \prod_{z<k \le j} x_k$, and after it
$0$, as the reference has them.  Forward saves both $x$ and $y$ on the
backward node.

members.name: cumsum_op
members.signature: int cumsum_op(const int & a, int axis)
members.summary: Inclusive cumulative sum along a single axis, $y_k = \sum_{j \le k} x_j$.
members.extended:
The output has the same shape and dtype as the input.  Backward
uses the reverse-cumsum trick to avoid an explicit $O(n^2)$
summation: reverse the upstream gradient along the axis, take its
cumsum, then reverse again.

**Math**

$$
  y_k = \sum_{j \le k} x_j, \qquad
  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x_i} =
  \sum_{j \ge i} \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial y_j}.
$$

**Shape**

Output shape equals `a.shape`.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Input tensor of any non-scalar shape and real dtype.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Axis along which to accumulate.  May be negative; in that case it is interpreted as `axis + ndim`.

returns.description: Output tensor of the same shape and dtype as `a`.

raises.description: If `a` is a scalar (`ndim == 0`) or `axis` is out of range.

notes:
Dispatch: Accelerate strided cumsum (CPU) / MLX `cumsum` (GPU).
Backward is `O(n)` per axis-stride.

members.name: det_op
members.summary: Compute $\det(A)$ for a square float tensor.
members.extended:
Validates that `a` is at least 2-D, square in the trailing two
dimensions, and float-typed; dispatches to the backend; and wires
`DetBackward` into the autograd graph (saving both $A$ and the
scalar output) when grad mode is active.

**Shape**

- `a`: `(..., N, N)`.
- Output: `(...,)` (rank decreases by 2; a single 2-D input
  yields a 0-D scalar).

**See Also**

parameters.description: Input matrix of shape `(..., N, N)`.

becomes available; the magnitude of `det` can over/underflow long

members.name: diagonal_op
members.signature: int diagonal_op(const int & a, int offset, int axis1, int axis2)
members.summary: Extract a single diagonal as a final-axis vector.
members.extended:
Returns the elements of `a` lying on the diagonal of the
`(axis1, axis2)` plane offset by `offset`: positive offsets shift
the diagonal toward the upper-right, negative offsets toward the
lower-left.  The two selected axes are removed and a new trailing axis
of length `L` is appended.

parameters.name: axis2
parameters.description: Second axis defining the plane.  Must differ from `axis1`; the two are canonicalised to `a1 < a2`.

returns.description: Tensor whose shape is `a.shape` with axes `axis1` and `axis2` removed and a trailing dimension of length $L = \max(0, \min(M - r_0, N - c_0))$ appended, where $M, N$ are the sizes of the two selected axes and $r_0, c_0$ are the starting row / column for the given offset.

notes:
Backward scatters the diagonal gradient into a zero tensor of the
original input shape, leaving off-diagonal positions zero.

members.name: dot_op
members.signature: int dot_op(const int & a, const int & b)
members.summary: Compute the dot product of two vectors or the matrix product of two matrices, with autograd support for both cases.
members.extended:
Dispatches on rank:

- **1-D × 1-D** — inner product
    $c = \sum_i a_i b_i$ producing a scalar (shape `{}`).
    Backed by Accelerate's `cblas_*dot` via the element-wise multiply
    and `reduce_sum` backend primitives.
    Backward node: `Dot1DBackward` (saves both operands).
  - **2-D × 2-D** — matrix product $C = A B$.
    Backed by `cblas_*gemm` (Accelerate) on CPU, `mlx::matmul` on GPU.
    Backward node: `Dot2DBackward` (saves both operands).

**Math**

1-D case:
$$
  c = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} a_i b_i, \qquad
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial a_i} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial c}\, b_i,
  \qquad
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial b_i} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial c}\, a_i
$$
2-D case:
$$
  C = A B, \qquad
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial A} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial C}\, B^\top,
  \qquad
  \frac{\partial L}{\partial B} = A^\top\, \frac{\partial L}{\partial C}
$$

**Shape**

- 1-D: `a.shape[0] == b.shape[0]`; output is rank-0.
- 2-D: `a.shape[1] == b.shape[0]`; output is $(M, N)$.

**References**

NumPy `numpy.dot` semantics for the 1-D and 2-D cases.

**See Also**

matmul_op : N-D matmul with NumPy broadcasting on batch dims.
inner_op : Last-axis contraction (NumPy `inner`).
outer_op : 1-D × 1-D outer product.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: Second operand.  Must have the same rank as `a`.

returns.description: - 1-D inputs → scalar tensor with shape `{}`. - 2-D inputs of shape $(M, K)$ and $(K, N)$ → matrix of shape $(M, N)$.

raises.description: If the contracted dimensions disagree (1-D length mismatch, or 2-D `a.shape[1] != b.shape[0]`).
If either input has rank other than 1 or 2.

notes:
Unlike `matmul_op` this entry point uses `AmpPolicy::KeepInput`
— integer dot products are valid and must not be promoted silently.

members.name: dropout_stateful_op
members.signature: int dropout_stateful_op(const int & x, const int & state_in, double p, bool training, Generator * gen)
members.summary: Stateful inverted dropout for the compile path — sibling of `dropout_op` that explicitly threads an MPSGraph-Philox state tensor as a second input and returns `(y, state_out)`.
members.extended:
In **eager mode** the function delegates to `dropout_op` for
the actual masking (so the result distribution matches the standard
dropout op identically) and returns a clone of `state_in` as the
state-out tensor — Lucid's eager `Generator` already
advances per call, so the state buffer is purely a placeholder
that exists for the trace recording.  Suppresses any nested tracer
recording from the inner `dropout_op` call so the trace contains
exactly one `"dropout_stateful"` op node (not a nested `"dropout"`
underneath it).

In the **compile path** the matching MPSGraph emitter consumes the
captured op node by calling
`randomTensorWithShape` — the 2-output
stateful Philox API — using `state_in` to seed the RNG and binding
the new state to `state_out`.  Across dispatches the state buffer
is rotated by the executable (either as an in/out feed pair or
promoted to an MPSGraph variable via
`compile_generic_fused_step_with_vars`), giving genuinely
per-dispatch varying masks where the stateless seed-only path
produces dispatch-deterministic ones.

parameters.name: state_in
parameters.description: Philox-4x32 state tensor (`int32[7]`).  Initial values are derived from Lucid's `Generator` on the Python side (one fresh state per dropout call site at trace time); the compile path mutates the buffer in-place across dispatches.

parameters.name: training
parameters.description: When `false`, the eager forward is a pass-through identity (the trace still records the op so the compile path can decide whether to emit the masked or identity branch).

parameters.name: gen
parameters.description: Optional explicit RNG used by the eager fallback; `nullptr` selects `default_generator()`.  Ignored by the compile path.

returns.description: `(y, state_out)` — masked output of the same shape and dtype as `x`; `state_out` is the same shape/dtype as `state_in` and (in eager mode) carries a verbatim clone of its contents.

members.name: eig_op
members.summary: Compute eigenvalues and right eigenvectors of a square float matrix.
members.extended:
**Math**

Returns $(w, V)$ such that $A V = V \mathrm{diag}(w)$, equivalently
$A v_i = w_i v_i$ for each column $v_i$ of $V$.

**Shape**

- Input `a`         : `(..., n, n)`
- Output `w`        : `(..., n)`
- Output `V`        : `(..., n, n)`

**See Also**

[[eigh_op]] : Symmetric / Hermitian specialisation (preferred when
              applicable — faster, real outputs, autograd-friendly).

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Square float tensor of shape `(..., n, n)`.  Leading dimensions are treated as independent batch axes — one decomposition per batch element.  Must be at least 2-D and floating-point.

returns.description: Two-element vector `{w, V}` where: - `w` has shape `(..., n)` — one eigenvalue per column of $A$ (real part only; see Notes on complex spectra). - `V` has shape `(..., n, n)` — columns are the right eigenvectors, normalised to unit Euclidean length.

raises.description: When `a` is not at least 2-D, not square, or not float-typed. Also if LAPACK fails to converge (rare; reported via `info > 0`).

examples:
In Python (via [[lucid.linalg.eig]]):
>>> A = lucid.tensor([[2.0, 0.0], [0.0, 3.0]])
>>> w, V = lucid.linalg.eig(A)
>>> w
Tensor([2., 3.])
notes:
Outputs are leaf nodes — autograd is **not** wired.  See header-level
Notes for the deferred backward formula and its caveats.

members.name: eigh_op
members.signature: int eigh_op(const int & a, const int & uplo)
members.summary: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a real symmetric square matrix.
members.extended:
**Math**

$A = V \mathrm{diag}(w) V^\top$ with $V^\top V = I$ and
$w_1 \le \cdots \le w_n$.

**Shape**

- Input `a`  : `(..., n, n)`, symmetric
- Output `w` : `(..., n)`, real, ascending
- Output `V` : `(..., n, n)`, orthonormal columns

**See Also**

[[eig_op]] : General non-symmetric eigendecomposition (use only
             when the symmetric structure cannot be exploited).

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Square float tensor of shape `(..., n, n)`, interpreted as symmetric.  Only the lower triangle is read; the strict upper triangle is ignored.  Leading dimensions are independent batch axes.  Must be at least 2-D and floating-point.

returns.description: Two-element vector `{w, V}` where: - `w` has shape `(..., n)` — real eigenvalues in **ascending** order. - `V` has shape `(..., n, n)` — columns are the orthonormal eigenvectors corresponding to `w`.

raises.description: When `a` is not at least 2-D, not square, or not float-typed. Also when LAPACK `*syevd` / `*heevd` fails to converge (reported via `info > 0`).

examples:
In Python (via [[lucid.linalg.eigh]]):
>>> A = lucid.tensor([[2.0, 1.0], [1.0, 2.0]])
>>> w, V = lucid.linalg.eigh(A)
>>> w
Tensor([1., 3.])
notes:
Outputs are leaf nodes — autograd is **not** wired.  See header-level
Notes for the closed-form backward and its caveats around sign
ambiguity / spectral degeneracy.

members.name: einsum_op
members.signature: int einsum_op(const int & pattern, const int & operands)
members.summary: General tensor contraction via an Einstein summation equation.
members.extended:
The equation uses the same syntax as NumPy's `einsum`: single-character
labels separated by commas for each input, optionally followed by `->`
and the output labels.  If `->` is omitted, the output labels are the
sorted set of labels that appear exactly once across all inputs (implicit
form).  Repeated labels in a single operand take the diagonal; labels
shared across operands trigger contraction; labels dropped from the output
are summed out.

**Math**

$$
  y_{\ell_\text{out}} = \sum_{\ell_\text{contract}}
      \prod_{k} x^{(k)}_{\ell^{(k)}}
$$

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Einsum equation, e.g. `"ij,jk->ik"` for matrix multiplication or `"bij,bjk->bik"` for batched matmul.

parameters.name: operands
parameters.description: The input tensors, one per comma-separated label group.  All operands must share the same device and dtype.

returns.description: Contracted tensor of the shape implied by the output labels.

raises.description: If the equation is malformed, label counts do not match operand dimensions, or contracted dimensions disagree in size.
If operands live on different devices.
If operands have different dtypes.

examples:
``"ij,jk->ik"``    — matrix multiplication.
``"bhij,bhjk->bhik"`` — multi-head batched attention contraction.
notes:
Ellipsis (`...`) is not yet supported.  Use explicit labels for batch
dimensions in the meantime.

members.name: equal_op
members.signature: int equal_op(const int & a, const int & b)
members.summary: Element-wise equality comparison.
members.extended:
Computes `out[i] = (a[i] == b[i])` for every element and returns the
result as a Bool tensor.  The comparison is exact, so for floating-point
inputs it follows IEEE 754 equality (`NaN == NaN` is false).

Non-differentiable: the comparison function has zero gradient almost
everywhere and undefined gradient on the decision boundary, so no
autograd node is registered and the output never carries grad.

**Math**

$$
  \mathrm{out}[i] = \mathbf{1}\!\left[a[i] = b[i]\right].
$$

**References**

NumPy `numpy.equal`.

**See Also**

not_equal_op, less_op, greater_op

parameters.name: a, b
parameters.description: Operands.  Must have identical shape, dtype, and device — this op does not broadcast.

returns.description: Bool tensor with the same shape as `a` and `b`.

raises.description: If the operand shapes, dtypes, or devices differ.

notes:
* Output dtype is always `Bool` regardless of input dtype.
* No broadcasting — callers must align shapes upstream.

members.name: fftn_op
members.signature: int fftn_op(const int & a, const int & n, const int & axes)
members.summary: N-dimensional complex-to-complex DFT (forward).
members.extended:
Computes the discrete Fourier transform of $x$ along the requested
`axes`.  This is the entry point invoked by `lucid.fft.fftn` and
is consumed by Python-side autograd machinery; this function itself
performs no gradient wiring.

**Math**

For a $d$-dimensional transform over axes $a_1, \dots, a_d$ of sizes
$N_1, \dots, N_d$,

$$
  X[k_1, \dots, k_d] = \sum_{n_1=0}^{N_1-1} \cdots \sum_{n_d=0}^{N_d-1}
    x[n_1, \dots, n_d] \,
    \exp\!\left( -2\pi i \sum_{j=1}^{d} \frac{k_j n_j}{N_j} \right) .
$$

The `"backward"` normalisation convention is used (no scaling on
forward; division by $\prod_j N_j$ on inverse).

**Shape**

`out.shape[axes[i]] == n[i]` when `n` is supplied; otherwise
`out.shape == a.shape`.  All other axes retain their input size.

**References**

Cooley & Tukey, "An Algorithm for the Machine Calculation of Complex
Fourier Series" (Math. Comp., 1965).

**See Also**

ifftn_op : Inverse N-D DFT (backward of `fftn`).
rfftn_op : Real-input N-D DFT.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Input tensor.  Real (F16/F32) inputs are accepted and promoted to C64; complex (C64) inputs are passed through.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Per-axis transform length.  When empty, the corresponding input dimensions are used.  When non-empty, `len(n) == len(axes)` must hold; each input axis is cropped or zero-padded to `n[i]`.

parameters.name: axes
parameters.description: Axes to transform.  Negative axes are normalised against the input rank.  Empty means "transform all axes".

returns.description: C64 tensor with shape equal to `a.shape()` except that each `axes[i]` is replaced by `n[i]` (or unchanged when `n` is empty).

raises.description: If `a` is null, rank-0, has an unsupported dtype, or if `len(n) != len(axes)` when `n` is non-empty.

notes:
FFT bypasses the IBackend dispatcher and calls MLX directly from
both CPU and GPU device paths (see `_Detail.h`).  On Device::CPU
the result is downloaded to host memory after the transform.

members.name: flatten_op
members.signature: int flatten_op(const int & a, int start_axis, int end_axis)
members.summary: Collapse a contiguous range of axes into a single dimension.
members.extended:
Folds dimensions `[start_axis, end_axis]` (inclusive on both ends) into
one axis whose size is the product of the collapsed dimensions.  Delegates
to `reshape_op` after computing the flattened size, so the input
must be contiguous along the affected range.

**Shape**

`(D_0, ..., D_{s-1}, D_s, ..., D_e, D_{e+1}, ..., D_{n-1})` becomes
`(D_0, ..., D_{s-1}, \prod_{d=s}^{e} D_d, D_{e+1}, ..., D_{n-1})`
with `s = start_axis` and `e = end_axis`.

**See Also**

`reshape_op`, `squeeze_all_op`.

parameters.name: start_axis
parameters.description: First axis in the range to collapse.  Supports negative indexing.

parameters.name: end_axis
parameters.description: Last axis in the range (inclusive).  Supports negative indexing. Must satisfy `start_axis <= end_axis` after normalisation.

returns.description: Tensor with rank `ndim - (end_axis - start_axis)` and a flattened dimension of size `\prod_{d=start_axis}^{end_axis} a.shape[d]` at position `start_axis`.

raises.description: If the collapsed range cannot be reshape-merged because of non-contiguous strides.

members.name: flip_op

members.summary: Reverse a tensor along one or more axes.
members.extended:

ordering is inverted.  Unlike `roll_op` there is no wrap-around.

returns.description: Tensor of the same shape and dtype as `a` with the requested axes reversed.

gradient — flipping is self-inverse.

members.name: forward_time_input
members.signature: int forward_time_input(const int & live, const int & values, const int & shape, const Edge & edge, int op_name, int input_idx)
members.summary: The tensor a node was handed at forward time, rebuilt — or `nullptr` when `live` still is that tensor.
members.extended:
`live` stopped being it when an in-place op that records a graph wrote
into it: the op gives it a grad_fn of its own.  The write moves its
version too, so this is reached past `check_version_match` only
when that check is waived (`is_mutation_on_saved_allowed`), or when
something gave `live` a grad_fn without writing into it — a custom
`Function` that returns its input (see
`Node::restore_saved_for_graph`).  The rebuilt tensor
holds the values the node saved by value and sits where `live` sat when
the node was recorded — on `edge`, the edge the node recorded for it —
so graph-mode backward computes what eager backward computes, and its own
derivative flows to what produced those values rather than to the write.

parameters.name: live
parameters.description: The tensor the node holds for graph-mode backward.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: What the node saved by value for the same input.  Empty when the node's formula does not read the input's values.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The input's shape at forward time.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: The edge the node recorded for the input.

parameters.name: op_name
parameters.description: Name of the op, for the error message.

parameters.name: input_idx
parameters.description: Zero-based index of the input within `op_name`.

returns.description: The rebuilt tensor; `nullptr` when `live` is still the tensor the node was handed, or when the node saved no values — its formula then reads `live` for its shape alone.

raises.description: `values` is not the whole input in one dtype, so there is nothing to rebuild it from.

$$

members.name: compile_metal_kernel
members.signature: MetalKernel compile_metal_kernel(const int & source, const int & function_name)
members.summary: Compile (or fetch from the global cache) a Metal compute pipeline.
members.extended:
Hashes `(source, function_name)` to form a cache key, then on
miss compiles `source` via `newLibraryWithSource:`, looks up
`function_name` inside the resulting library, and creates a
`MTLComputePipelineState` + dedicated `MTLCommandQueue`.

**See Also**

`run_metal_kernel` — invokes the compiled pipeline.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Complete MSL source text containing at least one `kernel` function named `function_name`.

parameters.name: function_name
parameters.description: The MSL kernel function symbol to bind.

returns.description: A valid kernel handle on success.  An invalid handle (`is_valid() == false`) is returned when Metal is unavailable (no GPU device on the host).

raises.description: On MSL compilation failure or pipeline-state creation error.

notes:
The pipeline cache is protected by an internal mutex, so concurrent
callers safely share compiled kernels.  Cached entries live for
the lifetime of the process.

members.name: deallocate_shared
members.summary: Release the Metal buffer held in `buf` and zero all fields.
members.extended:
Drops the `CFRetain` on `buf.mtl_handle` and clears the
descriptor in place so callers cannot reuse the dangling pointer
by accident.  Calling this on a zero-initialised `MetalBuffer`
is a no-op (safe).

parameters.name: buf
parameters.description: The descriptor to release.  Mutated to the zero state.

notes:
Marked `noexcept` — failures from the underlying Obj-C release
are silently swallowed because there is no recoverable action.

members.name: download_gpu_to_cpu
members.signature: CpuStorage download_gpu_to_cpu(const GpuStorage & gpu, const int & shape)
members.summary: Download a GPU array to a freshly allocated CPU buffer.
members.extended:
Calls `arr.eval()` to force materialisation of any pending lazy
MLX kernels, then `memcpy`s the contiguous data into a new
`CpuStorage` of the requested shape.

parameters.name: gpu
parameters.description: Source MLX-backed storage on the GPU stream.

returns.description: A fresh CPU buffer.  Disjoint from the GPU source — mutations do not propagate either way.

notes:
Always synchronous from the caller's perspective.  The cost is
dominated by the GPU graph completion (the actual `memcpy` is
at ~100 GB/s).

members.name: evaluate_pending
members.summary: Evaluate every GPU array still waiting to run, and return how many.
members.extended:
Lucid's Metal path is lazy: an op records a graph node and returns, and
nothing runs until a value is read.  `lucid.metal.synchronize()`
promises the queued work is done, but MLX keeps no list of unevaluated
arrays, so `wrap_mlx_array` notes each one it wraps (as a weak
reference that never keeps it alive) and this runs whichever are still
alive and unevaluated.

raises.description: When an array cannot be evaluated (an allocation past the device's buffer limit, a kernel that refuses its arguments).  The others still run first; then the first failure is raised, its message prefixed with the count of failures.  A `LucidError` subclass keeps its class, MLX's `std::invalid_argument` becomes `InvalidArgument`, and any other `std::exception` a `LucidError`.

members.summary: Allocate a shared Metal buffer wrapped in an RAII owner.

members.name: run_metal_kernel
members.signature: int run_metal_kernel(const MetalKernel & kernel, const int & inputs, const int & output_shape, Dtype output_dtype, const KernelLaunchConfig & config, const int & constants)
members.summary: Encode + dispatch a compiled kernel; block until it completes.
members.extended:
Allocates an output `SharedStorage` of `output_shape` /
`output_dtype`, binds `inputs` at indices `0..n-1`,
`constants` at `n..n+k-1`, and the output buffer at `n+k`,
then dispatches the threadgroup grid given by `config` and waits
synchronously for the GPU to finish.

**See Also**

`compile_metal_kernel` — produces `kernel`.
`make_metal_shared` — backs the returned storage.

parameters.name: kernel
parameters.description: Compiled pipeline produced by `compile_metal_kernel`. Must satisfy `kernel.is_valid() == true`.

parameters.name: inputs
parameters.description: Input tensors.  `SharedStorage` is bridged in place; `GpuStorage` is materialised (`eval()`) and copied into a fresh shared buffer; `CpuStorage` is copied verbatim.

parameters.description: Logical shape of the output tensor.

parameters.name: output_dtype
parameters.description: Element dtype of the output tensor.

parameters.name: constants
parameters.description: Scalar constants bound after the input buffers.  Defaults to an empty list.

returns.description: `SharedStorage` backed by a unified-memory buffer; the result is immediately CPU-readable on return (the call waits for completion).

raises.description: If the kernel is invalid, an input type cannot be resolved, or the GPU dispatch fails.

notes:
Returning `SharedStorage` (rather than `GpuStorage`) trades
some bandwidth for caller flexibility — the result can flow into
either CPU or GPU consumers without an extra copy.

members.name: settle_buffer_readers
members.signature: void settle_buffer_readers(const SharedStorage & sh, int with)
members.summary: Run every pending GPU array whose graph reads `sh`'s bytes, then wait for the device, so a host write into `sh` that follows changes none of them.

parameters.name: sh
parameters.description: The buffer about to be written.

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: Arrays to run in the same pass — the value about to be written, which would otherwise cost a second trip to the device.

notes:
A pending array reads the buffer when its graph reaches an array that has
run and holds the buffer's bytes: the pinned alias (`sh.gpu_alias`), a
DLPack import of the same Metal buffer, or whatever MLX derived from either
without a copy (reshape, slice, contiguous, copy, single-input cat/stack,
unit-axis sum).  Only arrays `wrap_mlx_array` noted as pending are
roots of the search.  Other pending work stays lazy while the walking it
costs stays within a budget shared by successive settles; past it every
pending array runs, which costs no more than searching it again on every
later write would.  Every op result `wrap_mlx_array` created that MLX
evaluated by aliasing the buffer's bytes (`copy_shared_buffer`) is then
rebound onto a fresh snapshot of the pre-write bytes before the write lands.

members.name: shared_storage_to_gpu
members.signature: GpuStorage shared_storage_to_gpu(const SharedStorage & sh, const int & shape)
members.summary: Adopt a unified-memory `SharedStorage` as a `GpuStorage` view.
members.extended:
Wraps the underlying `MTLResourceStorageModeShared` buffer as a
fresh MLX array without copying.  The result is readable + writable
from both CPU and GPU (subject to Metal's memory-model rules).

parameters.name: sh
parameters.description: Source storage backed by a shared Metal buffer.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Logical shape to view the buffer with.

returns.description: A non-copying view participating in MemoryTracker accounting.  It shares `sh.version` with the CPU view.

notes:
When `sh` is pinned the result is a copy of `sh.gpu_alias` (reshaped
if `shape` differs), so MLX never sees it as the buffer's sole owner and
cannot donate the buffer to an op's output.  This is the canonical fast
path for results produced by `run_metal_kernel` that flow back into
MLX-based ops.

members.name: upload_cpu_to_gpu
members.signature: GpuStorage upload_cpu_to_gpu(const CpuStorage & cpu, const int & shape)
members.summary: Upload a CPU buffer to GPU-private memory via `mlx::core::copy`.
members.extended:
MLX arrays own GPU-private pages that **cannot alias** a CPU
pointer (touching the raw `data()` from the CPU side raises
SIGBUS on M-series hardware).  This routine allocates a new MLX
array of the requested shape and dispatches a lazy
`mlx::core::copy` from the CPU buffer.  The `cpu` storage is
kept alive — via a custom deleter on the source MLX view — until
the asynchronous copy completes.

**See Also**

`download_gpu_to_cpu` — inverse direction.
`shared_storage_to_gpu` — zero-copy variant for shared buffers.

parameters.description: Source buffer in Accelerate-allocated CPU memory.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Logical shape of the array.  Must match `cpu` element count.

returns.description: A GPU-resident array participating in MemoryTracker accounting.

notes:
Copy bandwidth on M-series unified memory is ~100 GB/s, so the
transfer is rarely the bottleneck — but the call still pays for a
fresh GPU allocation.  Prefer batching uploads.

members.name: histc_op
members.signature: int histc_op(const int & a, int bins, double lo, double hi)
members.summary: Histogram counts over $[\mathrm{lo}, \mathrm{hi})$ with `bins` uniform buckets.
members.extended:
Composite — counts-only wrapper around `histogram_op`.  When
`lo == hi` the range is auto-derived from the input via `min_op`
and `max_op`, with the degenerate `min == max` case bumped by
$+1$ so the bins remain well-defined (matches reference framework
behaviour).  Not differentiable — integer-valued output.

**Math**

Let $w = (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) / \mathrm{bins}$.  Then for each
bin index $k \in [0, \mathrm{bins})$,
$$
  y_k = \#\!\left\{\, i : \mathrm{lo} + k w \le a_i < \mathrm{lo} + (k+1) w \,\right\}
$$

**See Also**

`histogram_op` — full version that also returns bin edges.

parameters.name: bins
parameters.description: Number of histogram bins.  Must be positive.

parameters.name: lo
parameters.description: Inclusive lower edge.  If `lo == hi`, auto-range from `min(a)` to `max(a)`.

returns.description: 1-D tensor of length `bins` holding integer counts.

raises.description: If `a` is null.

notes:
Values outside `[lo, hi)` are dropped silently by the underlying
`histogram_op` — no overflow / underflow bins are returned.

members.name: histogram2d_op
members.signature: int histogram2d_op(const int & a, const int & b, int bins_a, int bins_b, double lo_a, double hi_a, double lo_b, double hi_b, bool density)
members.summary: Compute a 2-D histogram from two equal-length 1-D tensors.
members.extended:
Treats paired observations `(a_k, b_k)` as samples on an
$\mathrm{bins\_a} \times \mathrm{bins\_b}$ grid of uniform rectangular
cells and counts the number of pairs falling in each cell.  When
`density` is true each cell value is divided by
`(step_a * step_b * N)`.

**See Also**

histogram_op : 1-D variant.
histogramdd_op : General N-dimensional variant.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: 1-D tensor of y-coordinates.  Must match `a` in length, dtype, and device.

parameters.name: bins_a
parameters.description: Number of bins along the x-axis.

parameters.name: bins_b
parameters.description: Number of bins along the y-axis.

parameters.name: density
parameters.description: If true, normalise to a probability density.

returns.description: `[counts, edges]` where `counts` has shape `(bins_a, bins_b)` and `edges` has shape `(bins_a + 1 + bins_b + 1,)` — the x-edges followed by the y-edges concatenated.  Both dtype F64.

notes:
Non-differentiable.  Executes on the CPU stream regardless of input
device.

members.name: histogram_op
members.signature: int histogram_op(const int & a, int bins, double lo, double hi, bool density)
members.summary: Compute a 1-D histogram of values in `a` over uniform bins.
members.extended:
Partitions the half-open interval $[lo, hi)$ into `bins` equal-width
sub-intervals and counts the number of elements of `a` falling in each
one.  When `density` is true the counts are normalised so that the
histogram integrates to one over the support: counts are divided by
`(bin_width * N)` where `N` is the total number of input elements.

**Math**

$$counts_i = \#\{k : lo + i \Delta \le a_k < lo + (i+1)\Delta\}, \quad
\Delta = (hi - lo) / bins$$

**See Also**

histogram2d_op : Joint 2-D histogram of paired observations.
histogramdd_op : Histogram of (N, D) row-major samples in D dimensions.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Input tensor of any shape; flattened internally.

parameters.name: bins
parameters.description: Number of equal-width bins.  Must be positive.

parameters.name: lo
parameters.description: Left edge of the lowest bin (inclusive).

parameters.name: hi
parameters.description: Right edge of the highest bin (exclusive, except for the last bin which is closed on the right).

parameters.name: density
parameters.description: If true, return a probability density; otherwise return raw counts.

returns.description: `[counts, edges]` where `counts` has shape `(bins,)` and `edges` has shape `(bins + 1,)`.  Both have dtype F64.

notes:
Non-differentiable: counts are piecewise-constant in the input.  Always
executes on the CPU stream; GPU inputs are copied across.

members.summary: Compute an N-dimensional histogram from a 2-D sample matrix.
members.extended:
Given an input tensor of shape `(N, D)` whose rows are D-dimensional
observations, partitions each dimension into the corresponding number
of bins and counts samples falling in each D-dimensional cell.  When
`density` is true each cell is divided by `(cell_volume * N)`.

**See Also**

histogram_op, histogram2d_op : Lower-dimensional specialisations.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: 2-D tensor of shape `(N, D)`; row `k` is the `k`-th sample.

parameters.name: bins
parameters.description: Length-D vector giving the bin count along each dimension.

parameters.name: ranges
parameters.description: Length-D vector of `(lo, hi)` pairs, one range per dimension.

parameters.name: density
parameters.description: If true, normalise to a probability density.

returns.description: `[counts, edges]` where `counts` is a D-dimensional tensor whose shape equals `bins`, and `edges` is a 1-D tensor of length `sum(bins[d] + 1)` containing the per-dimension edge arrays concatenated in order.  Both dtype F64.

notes: Non-differentiable.  Always executes on the CPU stream.

members.name: holds_saved_values
members.summary: Whether a node kept an input's values for backward in the slot `s`.
members.extended:
The one rule that decides both which inputs a node's version check guards
(`AutogradNode::validate_versions`) and which ones graph-mode
backward can rebuild (`forward_time_input`).  A backward that reads
an input's values saves them, by value, in that input's slot; an empty
slot means the formula reads the input's shape at most, so a write into
the input after forward cannot change the gradient and is not refused —
the reference's rule for `add`, `sum` or a view.  Checking every input
instead refused `y[:, 1] = y[:, 0] + 5` on the CPU, where the slice is a
view whose version the write moves.  A zero-element input saves no bytes
and is not guarded either: no write can change what it holds.

members.name: householder_product_op
members.signature: int householder_product_op(const int & H, const int & tau)
members.summary: Materialise the orthogonal $Q$ from packed Householder reflectors.
members.extended:
**Math**

$$
  Q = H_1 H_2 \cdots H_k, \qquad k = \min(m, n)
$$

**Shape**

- Input `H`    : `(m, n)`
- Input `tau`  : `(k,)` with $k = \min(m, n)$
- Output `Q`   : `(m, k)`

**References**

LAPACK `*orgqr`; Golub & Van Loan §5.1.2.

**See Also**

[[eig_op]]  : Produces packed reflectors for general eigenvector
              reconstruction.
[[eigh_op]] : Symmetric eigendecomp; reflectors come from a
              tridiagonal reduction step.

parameters.name: H
parameters.description: Packed reflector matrix of shape `(m, n)` produced by a QR-type factorisation.  Column $i$ stores reflector $v_i$ in the strict lower triangle below the diagonal (the diagonal entry of $v_i$ is implicitly $1$ and the slot is reused for $R$).  Must be float-typed and non-null.

parameters.name: tau
parameters.description: 1-D scaling factors of length $k = \min(m, n)$.  `tau[i]` is the $\tau_i$ scalar of the $i$-th reflector $H_i = I - \tau_i v_i v_i^\top$.  Must be float-typed and non-null.

returns.description: Explicit orthogonal matrix $Q$ of shape `(m, k)` with the same dtype as `H`.  Columns are orthonormal ($Q^\top Q = I_k$).

raises.description: When `H` or `tau` is null / not float-typed.

notes:
Output is a leaf node — autograd is **not** wired.  Gradients flow
through the calling QR / eig op rather than through this unpack
step.

members.name: hstack_op
members.summary: Horizontally stack a sequence of tensors.
members.extended:
Equivalent to NumPy `hstack`: for 1-D inputs the result concatenates
along axis 0; for tensors with rank >= 2 the concatenation occurs along
axis 1.  Tensors must agree on every non-horizontal dimension.

**See Also**

`vstack_op`, `concatenate_op`.

parameters.name: xs
parameters.description: Non-empty list of tensors with the same rank, dtype, and device.

returns.description: Horizontally concatenated tensor.

examples:
1-D inputs ``[a, b, c]`` and ``[d, e]`` produce ``[a, b, c, d, e]``.
2-D inputs of shapes ``(R, C_i)`` produce shape ``(R, \sum_i C_i)``.

members.name: huber_loss_op
members.signature: int huber_loss_op(const int & input, const int & target, double delta, int reduction)
members.summary: Public Huber (smooth L1) loss entry point.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Ground-truth tensor of the same shape.

parameters.name: delta
parameters.description: Quadratic / linear transition threshold; must be `> 0`.

returns.description: Reduced or per-element loss tensor.

members.name: hypot_op
members.signature: int hypot_op(const int & a, const int & b)
members.summary: Pythagorean length: $y = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$.
members.extended:
Composite over `square_op` + `add_op` + `sqrt_op`.
**Naive** formulation — does not perform IEEE-754 overflow-safe scaling
(i.e. no $\max(|a|, |b|) \cdot \sqrt{1 + (\min / \max)^2}$ trick),
matching the engine's `square_op` precision.

**Math**

$$
  y = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}
$$

returns.description: Tensor on the broadcast shape; values $\ge 0$.

notes:
Inputs near the float dtype's overflow threshold may lose precision —
prefer a dedicated `hypot` kernel for safety-critical paths.

members.name: ifftn_op
members.signature: int ifftn_op(const int & a, const int & n, const int & axes)
members.summary: N-dimensional inverse complex-to-complex DFT (forward of the inverse).
members.extended:
Inverts an N-D DFT.  Uses the `"backward"` normalisation
convention: forward has no scaling, this op divides by $\prod_j N_j$
where $N_j$ is the transform length along each axis.

**Math**

$$
  x[n_1, \dots, n_d] = \frac{1}{\prod_j N_j}
    \sum_{k_1=0}^{N_1-1} \cdots \sum_{k_d=0}^{N_d-1}
    X[k_1, \dots, k_d] \,
    \exp\!\left( +2\pi i \sum_{j=1}^{d} \frac{k_j n_j}{N_j} \right) .
$$

**See Also**

fftn_op : Forward N-D DFT.
irfftn_op : Inverse of the real-input DFT.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Input tensor.  C64 expected; F16/F32 are accepted and promoted.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Per-axis transform length.  Empty means "use input sizes". When supplied, `len(n) == len(axes)` is required.

parameters.name: axes
parameters.description: Axes to transform.  Negative values are normalised against the input rank.  Empty means "transform all axes".

returns.description: C64 tensor of the same shape as `a` (with `axes[i]` replaced by `n[i]` when `n` is supplied).

raises.description: If `a` is null, rank-0, has an unsupported dtype, or if `len(n) != len(axes)` when `n` is non-empty.

notes:
FFT bypasses IBackend dispatch and calls MLX directly from both CPU
and GPU device paths (see `_Detail.h`).

members.name: in_range_mask_storage
members.signature: int in_range_mask_storage(const int & s, double lo, double hi, int numel, Dtype dt, Device device, bool inclusive)
members.summary: Mask elements that fall inside the closed range `[lo, hi]`.
members.extended:
Returns `1` where `lo <= s <= hi` and `0` everywhere else, used
by clamp / hardtanh backward passes to gate the gradient through the
active region.

returns.description: New storage holding the {0, 1} gate.

members.name: index_select_op
members.signature: int index_select_op(const int & a, int dim, const int & indices)
members.summary: Pick `indices.size` slices along `dim` of `a`.
members.extended:
Composite over `reshape_op` + `expand_op` + `gather_op`.
The 1-D index list is reshaped to rank `a.ndim` (size $k$ along `dim`,
1 elsewhere) and expanded to the source shape so `gather_op`'s
same-rank contract holds.

**Math**

For each output coordinate $(\ldots, j, \ldots)$ along `dim`:
$$
  y_{\ldots, j, \ldots} = a_{\ldots, \mathrm{idx}_j, \ldots}
$$

**See Also**

`take_op` — flat indexing; `narrow_op` — contiguous window.

parameters.name: dim
parameters.description: Axis to index along.  Negative values wrap modulo `a.ndim`.

returns.description: Tensor with the same shape as `a` except size $k$ along `dim`.

raises.description: If `dim` is out of range.
If `indices` is not 1-D or not an integer dtype.

members.name: inner_op
members.signature: int inner_op(const int & a, const int & b)
members.summary: Compute the generalised inner product of $A$ and $B$ by contracting their last axes (NumPy `inner` semantics).
members.extended:
For rank-$n_A$ and rank-$n_B$ inputs whose last dims agree in size, the
output preserves all leading-of-A dims followed by all leading-of-B
dims, with the shared last axis summed out.

**Math**

General contraction over the trailing axis ($K = a_{n_A-1} = b_{n_B-1}$):
$$
  \mathrm{out}[i_0, \ldots, i_{n_A-2}, j_0, \ldots, j_{n_B-2}]
    = \sum_{k=0}^{K-1}
        A[i_0, \ldots, i_{n_A-2}, k]\,
        B[j_0, \ldots, j_{n_B-2}, k]
$$
2-D × 2-D specialisation:
$$
  \mathrm{out}[i, j] = \sum_k A[i, k]\, B[j, k]
$$

**Shape**

- `a.shape[-1] == b.shape[-1]` is required.
- Output shape concatenates the all-but-last dims of each input.

**References**

NumPy `numpy.inner` (which Lucid mirrors).

**See Also**

dot_op : 1-D × 1-D / 2-D × 2-D specialised dispatch.
matmul_op : Standard matmul with NumPy batch broadcasting.
outer_op : 1-D outer product (the rank-1 "anti-inner").
einsum_op : The lowering target for the gradient-tracked path.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: First operand, rank $\ge 1$.  Last dim is the contraction axis.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: Second operand, rank $\ge 1$.  Last dim must match `a.shape[-1]`.

returns.description: Output with shape `a.shape[:-1] + b.shape[:-1]`.  When both inputs are 1-D the result is a scalar (shape `{}`).

raises.description: If either input is rank-0 or the last dims disagree.

notes:
When gradient tracking is enabled this op is lowered to `einsum_op`
with a pattern produced by `inner_einsum_pattern` (free axes of $A$
use letters `a..o`, free axes of $B$ use `p..y`, contracted axis
is `z`).  The einsum backward pass handles autograd, so this op has
no dedicated backward node.

On the GPU stream the output shape is read back from the MLX array
after the kernel returns to absorb any scalar-squeeze MLX may perform.

members.name: adopt_graph_position
members.signature: bool adopt_graph_position(const int & a, const int & out)
members.summary: Move `out`'s place in the autograd graph onto `a`.
members.extended:
`fwd_fn` builds a differentiable `out` whose grad_fn knows how to
undo this op.  Taking only its storage kept the new numbers and threw
the derivative away, so `a` still sat where it was before the call
and reported the gradient of whatever produced it:

y = x * 1.0; y.exp_(); y.sum().backward()  ->  dx = 1
                                    reference  ->  dx = exp(x)

Silent, in both families: the value was right and only the derivative
was not, so a model using one trained on a wrong gradient with nothing
to show for it.  The views of `a` read the values it now holds, so
they move with it.

The version moves too, as for any write.  A node that saved `a` before
the write holds a tensor whose values and grad_fn are no longer the ones
it saw; with the count left alone nothing told it so.  Eager backward of
an engine node got away with that, reading the Storage it had saved, but
graph-mode backward read the written values, and a custom `Function`
reads its saved tensors as they are, with the count the only sign of the
write: `y = Fn.apply(x); y.mul_(2)` gave the gradient of the written
`y` on both devices.  The op's own node is not among those that
refuse: it was handed a snapshot (`snapshot`), a tensor of its own
whose count no write to `a` reaches.

The hooks registered on `a` stay on its old slot, as the reference's do:
they were asked about the values before the write.  `retain_grad` follows
the tensor to its new slot.

members.name: detach_and_bump
members.summary: What to do when there was no graph position to adopt.
members.extended:
Nothing to adopt means the op is not differentiable — `ceil`,
`floor`, `round` and `sign` all end the graph.  `a`'s contents
no longer depend on what they were, so leaving its old grad_fn in place
answers with the gradient of whatever produced `a`, unchanged.  Cut
it, which is the out-of-place convention — and cut its views with it,
since they read the same constant values.

Only under an active GradMode: inside `no_grad` the write is an
ordinary mutation of a tensor belonging to a graph built earlier, and
severing it there would lose a chain the caller means to keep — the
version counter guards that case, and it still runs.

members.name: rebase_views
members.summary: Re-derive the other members of `a`'s view family after a write through `a`.
members.extended:
Every member reads one run of the buffer, as `a` does, so the write
changed exactly the part of each member the two runs share.  Autograd has
to say so, or the member sends its gradient to the values the write
replaced:

* a member the write missed keeps its values, and so its graph;
* a member the write covered reads only `a`'s values now — a reshape of
  `a` when the runs are the same, a run of `a` otherwise — and when
  `a` does not require grad it is cut from the graph, since those are a
  constant's values;
* a member the write reached into has `a`'s part spliced into its old
  graph by a CopySlices node, as the reference does for the base of a
  written slice.  When `a` does not require grad, that part just stops
  passing gradient back.

A leaf that requires grad keeps its place and only its values move: the
write was into its base or beside it, since `write_through` refuses one
through a view of it while autograd records.

members.name: records_graph
members.signature: bool records_graph(const int & a, const int & other)
members.summary: Whether the op about to run records a node — and so keeps a handle on `a` and on `other`, the second operand of a binary op.  `other` is what makes `buf.mul_(v)` record a node when only `v` requires grad.

members.name: refuse_on_leaf
members.signature: void refuse_on_leaf(const int & a, const char * name)
members.summary: Refuse to mutate a leaf that requires grad.
members.extended:
A leaf is where gradient accumulates, and an in-place write moves it
without leaving anything behind that says so.  Nor is there a right
number to return: after the write `x` *is* the result, so "the
gradient with respect to x" names two different tensors depending on
when it is asked.  The reference refuses the same setup for the same
reason.  Callers that mean to overwrite say so with `no_grad`, which
is what every optimiser step already does.

`is_leaf()`, not `!grad_fn()`: a leaf that has taken part in a
forward carries its gradient accumulator as `grad_fn`, so the old test
stopped refusing the moment a parameter was first used — every in-place
op on a trained parameter then went through, and the ones that rebind
turned the parameter into a non-leaf that never received `.grad`.

members.name: run
members.summary: Run an in-place op: `forward()` computes the result from a stand-in for `a` (`snapshot`), and `write_result` makes it `a`'s values.
members.extended:
Autocast does not apply to an in-place op, as the reference's does not,
so the op computes in `a`'s own dtype.  The forward used to take the
op's AMP policy as an out-of-place call does, and the write then gave
`a` the result's dtype: under `autocast(metal, float16)`,
`x.mul_(y)` of two float32 tensors left `x` float16 (an optimiser's
parameter among them), and `x.exp_()` of a float16 `x` left it
float32.  Casting the result back keeps the dtype but not the values: the
float32 product would be rounded through float16 first, where the
reference computes it in float32.

members.name: snapshot
members.signature: int snapshot(const int & a, const int & other)
members.summary: A stand-in for `a` to run the forward against.
members.extended:
A node keeps a handle on each tensor it was given, and graph-mode
backward reads its values and its graph position through that handle,
not through the Storage it saved by value.  Handed `a` itself, the node
read `a` as the write left it — the new values, and the new grad_fn,
which is the node itself:

sin_                ->  cos(sin(x)) instead of cos(x)
    buf.mul_(v)         ->  d/dv = buf * v instead of buf

in graph mode only, since eager `backward()` reads the Storage.  So
whenever the op records a node, the node is handed a tensor of its own:
one that holds the values `a` holds now and sits where `a` sits now.
`a` not requiring grad is no exception — the other operand of a binary
op may, and its node saves this one.  Being its own tensor, it also keeps
its own version count, which is what lets the write move `a`'s
(`adopt_graph_position`) without the node refusing itself.

The snapshot shares the buffer rather than copying it, and the caller's
assignment replaces `a`'s *slot* rather than the buffer, so the
original values stay alive and unmutated for as long as the node needs
them.  No data is copied, and when no node is recorded — `no_grad`, or
no operand requiring grad — nothing is allocated either.

A write that lands in the buffer (`TensorImpl::write_lands_in_buffer`:
a CPU tensor with live views, or one read from `.grad`) is the
exception: a node holding the buffer would read the new values back, and
the holder would stop the write besides — `p.grad.add_(w)` with `w`
requiring grad was refused as a gradient something else reads.  Its
snapshot is a copy.

members.name: write_result
members.signature: int write_result(const int & a, int out, const char * name)
members.summary: Make `out`, an in-place op's result, the values of `a`; return `a`.
members.extended:
Every engine in-place op's result lands here (through `run`), so
what holds for all of them is held once:

* the shape does not change — the live views of `a` read it;
* nor does the dtype.  `out` is cast to `a`'s dtype when the
  reference's in-place rule allows it (`lucid._promotion.can_cast`: a
  write may narrow within a kind but never move down bool < integer <
  floating < complex), and the op is refused otherwise, `a` untouched.
  Taking `out`'s dtype instead, `int64.exp_()` turned the tensor into
  float32 where the reference raises;
* `a` takes `out`'s place in the graph (`adopt_graph_position`),
  or leaves it when `out` has none (`detach_and_bump`).

members.name: dlpack_to_metal
members.summary: Adopt a `kDLMetal` DLPack tensor as a Lucid GPU tensor.
members.extended:
Wraps the incoming `MTLBuffer` in a fresh `mlx::core::array`
without copying.  Per the DLPack contract the consumer owns `managed`
from this point: its `deleter` is called when the last reference to
the resulting tensor's storage dies, not before, so the producer's
buffer outlives every view Lucid hands out.

parameters.name: managed
parameters.description: Tensor to adopt.  Must be `kDLMetal` and contiguous.

returns.description: A leaf tensor sharing the producer's pages.

raises.description: Wrong device, unsupported dtype, or non-contiguous strides.  The `deleter` is invoked before raising so the producer is not leaked by a rejected import.

members.name: metal_to_dlpack
members.summary: Export a Metal-resident tensor as a `kDLMetal` DLPack tensor.
members.extended:
The returned block is heap-allocated and owns a reference to the
source `mlx::core::array`, so the buffer stays alive for exactly as
long as the capsule does regardless of what happens to the Lucid tensor
meanwhile.  Ownership passes to the caller, who must either invoke
`deleter` or hand the block to a DLPack consumer that will.

parameters.name: impl
parameters.description: Tensor to export.  Must be on `Device::GPU`.

returns.description: Never null; failures raise instead.

raises.description: `impl` is null, lives on the CPU, or has a dtype with no DLPack spelling on Metal (`float64` among them — Metal has no such type, so there is nothing to point a consumer at).

members.signature: int interpolate_nearest_2d_op(const int & input, int H_out, int W_out)

$$
(clamped to valid index ranges).  A backward node is attached.

returns.description: Resampled tensor of shape `(N, C, H_out, W_out)`.
